*vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.flashinfer_mxint4_moe.flashinfer_trtllm_mxint4_moe*

flashinfer_trtllm_mxint4_moe(x, router_logits, w13_weight_packed,
    w13_weight_scale, w2_weight_packed, w2_weight_scale, global_num_experts,
    top_k, intermediate_size_per_partition, local_num_experts, ep_rank=0,

    routing_method_type=None, routing_replay_out=None)

    Parameters: ~

            Input hidden states. dtype: bfloat16

        router_logits (Tensor)

        w13_weight_packed (Tensor)
            Packed gate+up weights. dtype: uint8

            Packed down weights. dtype: uint8

            Scales for down weights. dtype: bfloat16

        top_k (int)
            Number of experts to select per token

        intermediate_size_per_partition (int)
            Intermediate size per partition

        local_num_experts (int)
            Number of experts on this rank

        ep_rank (int, default: 0)
            Expert parallelism rank (default: 0)

        num_expert_group (int | None, default: None)
            Number of expert groups (default: None -> 0)

        topk_group (int | None, default: None)
            Top-k within groups (default: None -> 0)

        routing_replay_out (Tensor | None, default: None)
            Optional buffer receiving the routing decisions so they can
            be replayed later

        e_score_correction_bias (Tensor | None, default: None)
            Optional routing bias. dtype: bfloat16

        routing_method_type (int | None, default: None)
            FlashInfer RoutingMethodType enum value

    Returns: ~
        Tensor
            Output tensor from MoE layer. dtype: same as x (bfloat16)

    TRT-LLM kernel using the shuffle + BlockMajorK layout variant.

    Returns 4D weight tensors in BlockMajorK layout (E, K/block_k, Mn,
    block_k)

*vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.flashinfer_utils._shuffle_mxfp8_moe_weights*

_shuffle_mxfp8_moe_weights(w13, w2, w13_scale, w2_scale, is_gated)
    Preprocess MXFP8 weights and scales for the FlashInfer TRT-LLM
    kernel.

    All three transforms (gate/up row reorder, `shuffle_matrix_a` weight
    shuffle, `shuffle_matrix_sf_a` scale shuffle) are fixed row/index
    permutations that depend only on the per-expert matrix shape, so the
    permutation is computed once and applied to every expert in a single
    gather instead of once per expert. `block_scale_interleave` accepts
    a batched `(E, M, K)` scale tensor directly. Output is bit-identical
    to the per-expert loop but ~20x faster (a 288-expert MoE otherwise
    costs seconds per layer at load).

*vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.flashinfer_utils.align_fp4_moe_weights_for_fi*

align_fp4_moe_weights_for_fi(w13, w13_scale, w2, w2_scale, is_act_and_mul,
    min_alignment=16)
    Pad intermediate size so FlashInfer kernels' alignment constraints
    hold.

    Some FlashInfer FP4 MoE kernels require the intermediate size used
    for GEMM to be divisible by a small alignment value. When this is
    not satisfied (e.g. with certain tensor-parallel sizes), we pad the
    gate/up and down projection weights along the intermediate dim.

*vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.flashinfer_utils.align_moe_weights_for_fi*

align_moe_weights_for_fi(w13, w2, is_act_and_mul, min_alignment=16)
    Pad intermediate size so FlashInfer kernels' alignment constraints
    hold.

    Some FlashInfer MoE kernels require the (gated) intermediate size
    used for GEMM to be divisible by a small alignment value. When this
    is not satisfied (e.g. with certain tensor-parallel sizes), we pad
    the gate/up and down projection weights along the intermediate dim.

*vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.flashinfer_utils.align_mxfp8_moe_weights_for_fi_trtllm*

align_mxfp8_moe_weights_for_fi_trtllm(w13, w2, w13_scale, w2_scale,
    is_act_and_mul, min_alignment, hidden_alignment)
    align_moe_weights_for_fi for MXFP8 weights and their UE8M0 block
    scales for the FlashInfer TRT-LLM MoE kernel, which also pads the
    hidden size to a multiple of hidden_alignment.

    Padded weights are zero and padded scales are 127 (UE8M0 for 1.0),
    so the padded rows and columns contribute nothing. Scales may be 3D
    [E, rows, cols] or flattened [E, rows * cols]; their layout is kept.
    Returns the padded intermediate and hidden sizes.

*vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.flashinfer_utils.convert_moe_weights_to_flashinfer_trtllm_block_layout*

convert_moe_weights_to_flashinfer_trtllm_block_layout(cache_permute_indices,
    w13_weight, w2_weight, is_gated_act_gemm=True)
    Convert expert weights to FlashInfer's block layout.

    This reorders W13 and W2 in place into the expected epilogue-tiled
    block layout and returns views of the shuffled weight tensors. Using
    one expert as scratch space avoids allocating another full copy of
    both weights.

*vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.flashinfer_utils.prepare_fp8_moe_layer_for_fi*

prepare_fp8_moe_layer_for_fi(layer, w13, w2, w13_scale, w13_input_scale,
    w2_scale, w2_input_scale, is_trtllm=False)
    Convert Fp8 MoE weights to flashinfer kernel format.

    Note that for trtllm we update the model state dict with the scale
    format needed for these kernels.

    Note that for per-tensor and for MXFP8 TRT-LLM, we update the
    layer's intermediate size (and for MXFP8 TRT-LLM its hidden size) if
    the weights needed padding.

*vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.flashinfer_utils.trtllm_nvfp4_hidden_alignment*

trtllm_nvfp4_hidden_alignment(per_token_activation, is_act_and_mul)
    Hidden-dim alignment for the TRTLLM-Gen NVFP4 MoE cubins.

    The per-token (dynamic activation scale) non-gated variant has far
    fewer tile configs for 256-aligned K and its heuristic default
    tactic fails with "No valid config found" (e.g. Nemotron's 2688 ->
    2816), so pad to 512.

*vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.fp8_utils._silu_mul_per_token_group_quant_fp8_colmajor*

    block of values and fills the outputs tensors at the right
    positions.

*vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.fp8_utils._upcast_e8m0_to_fp32*

_upcast_e8m0_to_fp32(scale)
    Upcast E8M0 (exponent-only) scale to float32.

    E8M0 stores only the 8-bit biased exponent (bias=127). To convert to
    float32 we place those 8 bits into the exponent field of an IEEE-754
    float32 (bits 23-30) with sign=0 and mantissa=0.

   *vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.fp8_utils.dequant_block_fp8*

dequant_block_fp8(weight, scale_inv, block_size, out_dtype=torch.float32)
    `[..., N, K]` fp8 x `[..., ceil(N/bn), ceil(K/bk)]` block scales ->
    `out_dtype`.

    Leading dimensions (e.g. the expert dimension) are batched. The
    product is computed in fp32, `out_dtype` only controls the final
    cast.

*vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.fp8_utils.dequantize_fp8_moe_weights*

dequantize_fp8_moe_weights(w13_weight, w13_scale, w2_weight, w2_scale, *,
    weight_key, num_w13_shards, weight_block_size, static_input_scales,
    out_dtype)
    Dequantize FP8 MoE weights for online requantization.

    Parameters: ~
        w13_weight (Tensor)
            `[E, num_w13_shards * I, K]` fp8 weights.

        w13_scale (Tensor)
            Per `weight_key`,
            `[E, num_w13_shards * ceil(I / bn), ceil(K / bk)]` (block),
            `[E, num_w13_shards]` (tensor, per expert and shard) or
            `[E, num_w13_shards * I]` / `[E, num_w13_shards * I, 1]`
            (channel).

        w2_weight (Tensor)
            `[E, K, I]` fp8 weights.

        w2_scale (Tensor)
            Per `weight_key`, `[E, ceil(K / bn), ceil(I / bk)]` (block),
            `[E]` (tensor) or `[E, K]` / `[E, K, 1]` (channel).

        weight_key (QuantKey)
            The weight quantization key, per-tensor, per-channel or
            block.

        num_w13_shards (int)
            2 for gated (w1, w3), else 1. Shards of a fused w13 with a
            single tensor scale are handled through the scale shape.

        weight_block_size (Sequence[int] | None)
            The `[bn, bk]` block shape, required for block scales.

        static_input_scales (bool)
            Whether the checkpoint has static activation scales, which
            are not supported: w1 and w3 share one input-scale slot,
            which the layerwise loader counts twice.

        out_dtype (dtype)
            The dequantized dtype.

    Returns: ~
        Iterator[tuple[slice, Tensor, Tensor]]
            An iterator of `(experts, w13, w2)` over groups of experts,
            bounding the

        Iterator[tuple[slice, Tensor, Tensor]]
            staging memory.

*vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.fp8_utils.get_w8a8_block_fp8_configs*

get_w8a8_block_fp8_configs(N, K, block_n, block_k) cached
    Return optimized configurations for the w8a8 block fp8 kernel. The
    return value will be a dictionary that maps an irregular grid of
    batch sizes to configurations of the w8a8 block fp8 kernel. To
    evaluate the kernel on a given batch size bs, the closest batch size
    in the grid should be picked and the associated configuration chosen
    to invoke the kernel.

*vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.fp8_utils.per_token_group_quant_fp8*

per_token_group_quant_fp8(x, group_size, eps=1e-10, dtype=None,
    column_major_scales=False, tma_aligned_scales=False, out_q=None,
    use_ue8m0=None)
    Function to perform per-token-group quantization on an input tensor
    `x`. It converts the tensor values into signed float8 values and
    returns the quantized tensor along with the scaling factor used for
    quantization.

    Parameters: ~
        x (Tensor)
            The input tensor with ndim >= 2.

        group_size (int)
            The group size used for quantization.

        eps (float, default: 1e-10)
            The minimum to avoid dividing zero.

        dtype (dtype | None, default: None)
            The dtype of output tensor. Note that only
            `torch.float8_e4m3fn` is supported for now.

        column_major_scales (bool, default: False)
            Outputs scales in column major.

        tma_aligned_scales (bool, default: False)
            Outputs scales in TMA-aligned layout.

        out_q (Tensor | None, default: None)
            Optional output tensor. If not provided, function will
            create.

        use_ue8m0 (bool | None, default: None)
            If True, round each scale down to a power of two (UE8M0
            format). None defers to the platform default.

    Returns: ~
        Tensor
            tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]: The quantized tensor and
            the

        Tensor
            scaling factor.

*vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.fp8_utils.requant_weight_ue8m0_inplace*

requant_weight_ue8m0_inplace(weight, weight_scale, block_size=(128, 128))
    Re-quantise weight so that its per-block scaling factors are in the
    UE8M0 (power-of-two) format expected by the new DeepGEMM kernels
    inplace.

    Parameters: ~
        weight (Tensor)
            Block-quantised weight tensor stored in
            `torch.float8_e4m3fn`. Expected shape `(..., M, K)`.

        weight_scale (Tensor)
            Corresponding per-block scale tensor (`torch.float32`) with
            shape `(..., M // block_size[0], K // block_size[1])`.

        block_size (Sequence[int], default: (128, 128))
            2-element iterable `[block_m, block_k]` describing the block
            quantisation granularity.

*vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.fp8_utils.silu_mul_per_token_group_quant_fp8_colmajor*

silu_mul_per_token_group_quant_fp8_colmajor(input, output=None,
    use_ue8m0=None, eps=1e-10, clamp_limit=None, group_size=128, alpha=1.0,
    beta=0.0, *, expert_ends=None, expert_alignment=0)
    Gated activation + block-fp8 quant. `alpha`/`beta` select the gate
    (silu: alpha=1, beta=0; swigluoai: alpha, beta from config).

    Optional expert endpoints follow DeepGEMM's prefix-sum layout.
    Padding values and scales are left unwritten and must not be
    consumed as live rows.

*vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.fp8_utils.silu_mul_quant_fp8_packed_triton*

silu_mul_quant_fp8_packed_triton(input, group_size=128, output_q=None,
    clamp_limit=None, alpha=1.0, beta=0.0, *, expert_ends=None,
    expert_alignment=0)
    Fuse activation and FP8 quantization, optionally skipping expert
    padding.

    `expert_ends` uses DeepGEMM's prefix-sum layout: each entry is the
    exclusive end of an expert's live rows, including earlier alignment
    gaps. An expert starts at the preceding end rounded up to
    `expert_alignment`. Padding outputs are left unwritten and must not
    be consumed as live rows. Without `expert_ends`, the original dense
    launch configuration is used and the metadata loads are compiled
    out.

*vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.gptq_utils.is_moe_layer_gptq_quantized*

is_moe_layer_gptq_quantized(prefix, quantized_layers)
    Whether the routed experts at `prefix` are quantized in the
    checkpoint.

    `prefix` is the absolute name of the fused expert layer
    (`...mlp.experts`), while `modules_in_block_to_quantize` names the
    individual expert projections (`...mlp.experts.0.down_proj`) or the
    fused expert module itself, using either absolute or block-relative
    names. Match on the `experts` portion of the name so that a layer
    whose experts are stored unquantized -- e.g. the MTP layer of a
    partially quantized checkpoint -- is not given a quantized method.

    Configs that enumerate no expert module at all say nothing about the
    experts, so the layer is assumed to be quantized.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------
                   *vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.lut_b_utils*

LUT-B weight format: 3-bit indices into per-tile E4M3 codebooks.

Rubin's `tcgen05.mma ... decompress::lut::b` instructions decode each
weight from a three-bit index into an eight-entry E4M3 codebook shared
by eight output channels. This module implements a calibration-free
format matching that contract. Each `8 (N) x 64 (K)` tile of a `[N, K]`
weight stores 192 bytes of packed three-bit indices (row-major over the
tile) and an eight-entry E4M3 codebook. Separately, every output channel
carries one UE8M0 scale per 32 K (`[N, K / 32]`), which is exactly the
hardware's block32 B scale, so the 16 scales of a tile may differ. They
keep small-magnitude rows and blocks out of the E4M3 subnormal range. In
total the format uses 3.375 bits per weight.

Functions: ~

dequantize_lut_b      Reconstruct the `[N, K]` or `[E, N, K]` weight from
                      LUT-B tiles.
lut_b_to_sm107_tiles  Rearrange stacked LUT-B weights into the SM107 MoE
                      kernel layout.
pack_lut_b_indices    Pack groups of eight 3-bit indices into three
                      little-endian bytes.
quantize_lut_b        Quantize a `[N, K]` or stacked `[E, N, K]` weight to
                      LUT-B.
unpack_lut_b_indices  Inverse of `pack_lut_b_indices`.

     *vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.lut_b_utils._block_errors*

_block_errors(blocks, exponent, tile_exponent, centers)
    Squared error of each K32 block, in units of the tile scale.

        *vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.lut_b_utils._fit_tiles*

_fit_tiles(values, weights, num_iterations)
    Fit one E4M3 codebook per row of `values` with weighted Lloyd
    iterations.

    Three initializations are tried and the lowest-error fit per tile is
    kept. Returns `(indices, centers, loss)`, where `loss` is the
    weighted squared error per tile.

*vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.lut_b_utils._normalize_centers*

_normalize_centers(centers, preserve_zero)
    Snap to E4M3, keep an exact zero where needed, and sort.

    *vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.lut_b_utils._refine_scales*

_refine_scales(blocks, exponent, tile_exponent, centers, num_rounds)
    Coordinate descent over block exponents and the tile codebook.

    Each round moves every block exponent by -1, 0 or +1, whichever
    decodes that block best with the current codebook, then refits the
    codebook for the new exponents. Each step is kept only where it
    lowers the error.

          *vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.lut_b_utils._rescale*

_rescale(blocks, exponent, tile_exponent)
    Per-tile values divided by their block scales, and Lloyd weights.

    Each value is weighed by its scale squared, relative to the tile
    scale, so a codebook fit minimizes the error of the rescaled
    weights.

   *vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.lut_b_utils._ue8m0_exponent*

_ue8m0_exponent(amax)
    Power of two that puts `amax` in (E4M3_MAX / 2, E4M3_MAX], as MXFP8.

  *vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.lut_b_utils.dequantize_lut_b*

dequantize_lut_b(packed, codebooks, scales, out_dtype=torch.bfloat16)
    Reconstruct the `[N, K]` or `[E, N, K]` weight from LUT-B tiles.

*vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.lut_b_utils.lut_b_to_sm107_tiles*

lut_b_to_sm107_tiles(packed, codebooks, scales)
    Rearrange stacked LUT-B weights into the SM107 MoE kernel layout.

    Returns `[E, N / 128, K / 128, 7168]` uint8. Each tile holds:

    - 6144 bytes of 3-bit indices, 48 bytes (K128) per output channel,
      in the no-swizzle K-major core-matrix layout (8 rows x 16 bytes),
    - 512 bytes of UE8M0 B scales: byte `q` of word `[lane][col]` is the
      scale of channel `col * 32 + lane` for K32 block `q`,
    - 512 bytes of codebooks: lane `g` holds the two eight-entry books
      (one per K64 half) of channel group `g`; lanes 16-31 are zero
      padding.

*vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.lut_b_utils.pack_lut_b_indices*

pack_lut_b_indices(indices)
    Pack groups of eight 3-bit indices into three little-endian bytes.

    *vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.lut_b_utils.quantize_lut_b*

quantize_lut_b(weight, *, num_iterations=LUT_B_LLOYD_ITERATIONS,
    num_scale_rounds=LUT_B_SCALE_ROUNDS,
    max_tiles_per_chunk=LUT_B_MAX_TILES_PER_CHUNK)
    Quantize a `[N, K]` or stacked `[E, N, K]` weight to LUT-B.

    Returns `(packed, codebooks, scales)` with shapes
    `[E, N/8, K/64, 192]` (uint8), `[E, N/8, K/64, 8]` (float8_e4m3fn)
    and `[E, N, K/32]` (uint8 UE8M0). The expert dim is dropped for 2D
    inputs.

    Each tile is fitted twice: once with its 16 block scales tied to one
    exponent for the whole tile, and once with each block's exponent
    taken from its own amax. Starting from the better fit,
    `num_scale_rounds` rounds of coordinate descent then adjust the
    block exponents and the codebook together. Every step only lowers
    the reconstruction error, so the result is never worse than a single
    scale per tile.

*vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.lut_b_utils.unpack_lut_b_indices*

unpack_lut_b_indices(packed)
    Inverse of `pack_lut_b_indices`.

*vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.marlin_utils.check_moe_marlin_supports_config*

    is zero-padded to a valid thread tile at weight prep (see
    marlin_moe_padded_intermediate), so only a group straddling the
    padded boundary stays unsupported. hidden_size is the MoE I/O extent
    and is never padded.

*vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.marlin_utils.marlin_moe_padded_intermediate*

marlin_moe_padded_intermediate(intermediate_size, group_size=-1)
    Smallest MoE intermediate size satisfying the Marlin MoE thread
    tiles.

    The kernel needs gate-up `2 * intermediate % 128 == 0` and down
    `intermediate % 64 == 0`, i.e. `intermediate % 64 == 0`. A
    misaligned size is zero-padded to the next valid tile at weight
    prep, kept a multiple of `group_size` so the group count stays
    integral. The padded region never reaches the MoE output: w13's
    padded output channels are zeroed by the zero-padded scales, so the
    padded inputs to w2 are zero.

   *vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.marlin_utils.marlin_pad_dim*

marlin_pad_dim(x, size, padded)

 *vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.marlin_utils.marlin_padded_nk*

marlin_padded_nk(size_n, size_k, group_size=-1)
    Minimal (padded_n, padded_k) satisfying a Marlin thread-tile family.

    Marlin GEMM and repack require (n % 64, k % 128) or (n % 128, k %
    64); shapes satisfying neither are zero-padded up to the cheaper
    family. K stays divisible by group_size so padded scales keep an
    integral group count. Padded weight regions contribute nothing to
    the GEMM output: quantized value 0 decodes to 0.0 (FP4/FP8) or is
    cancelled by the zero-padded scales/zero-points (INT).

*vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.marlin_utils_fp4.nvfp4_marlin_process_scales*

nvfp4_marlin_process_scales(marlin_scales, scale_factor=None, a_dtype=None)
    Process NVFP4 weight scales into the special S0E5M3 format for
    Marlin.

    Parameters: ~
        marlin_scales (Tensor)
            Weight scales tensor in half precision, already permuted for
            the Marlin kernel layout.

        scale_factor (float | None, default: None)
            Optional power-of-2 rescaling factor. If None, the factor is
            computed automatically so that every non-zero scale
            satisfies `scale * 2^7 >= 2` (i.e., the MSB of the S0E5M3
            representation is always 1). When provided (e.g., for MoE
            layers where all experts must share the same factor), the
            given value is used directly. The caller is responsible for
            dividing `global_scale` by the returned `scale_factor` to
            preserve numerical correctness.

        a_dtype (dtype | None, default: None)
            dtype of the activations the scales will be used with. None
            keeps the dtype of `marlin_scales`.

    Returns: ~
        tuple[Tensor, float]
            A tuple of (processed_scales, scale_factor).

*vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.marlin_utils_fp4.prepare_moe_mxfp4_layer_for_marlin*

prepare_moe_mxfp4_layer_for_marlin(layer, w13, w2, w13_scale, w2_scale,

    *vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.mxfp4_utils.mxfp4_quantize*

mxfp4_quantize(x)
    Quantize a bf16/fp16 tensor to MXFP4 along its last dimension.

    Dispatches to the fastest backend available on the current platform:

    - the native XPU custom op on XPU,
    - aiter on ROCm when `aiter` is installed,
    - and the portable Triton kernel (`downcast_to_mxfp`) otherwise.

    Returns packed FP4 values (uint8, two values per byte) and per-block
    (group-32) e8m0 scales (uint8).

*vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.mxfp4_utils.should_use_cdna4_mx_scale_swizzle*

should_use_cdna4_mx_scale_swizzle()
    Whether to use the CDNA4 swizzled scale layout for mxfp4 on gfx950.

    CDNA4 swizzle requires BLOCK_K%256==0; at TP>=4 the A8W4 dispatch
    picks BK<256 tiles for the smaller per-rank shapes, so swizzle must
    be off. Used by both the weight-load swizzle in `_swizzle_mxfp4` and
    the kernel-argument gate in `aiter_mxfp4_w4a8_moe`; they must agree.

    Naive MXFP8 quantization. For each block of 32 elements along the

*vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.mxfp8_utils._mxfp8_quant_triton_kernel*

_mxfp8_quant_triton_kernel()
    Lazily-built Triton kernel: per-32-block E8M0 scale + FP8-E4M3
    quant.

    Fuses what `_mxfp8_e4m3_quantize_torch` does in several elementwise
    passes into one launch. Each program handles `[BLOCK_M, BLOCK_K]`,
    i.e. BLOCK_K / 32 MX blocks of BLOCK_M rows, so rows are read in

*vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.mxfp8_utils.mxfp8_e4m3fn_to_e4m3fnuz*

mxfp8_e4m3fn_to_e4m3fnuz(w, scale)
    Reinterpret MXFP8 e4m3fn weights as e4m3fnuz without changing
    values.

    The same bits read as fnuz are worth half, so each E8M0 exponent
    goes up by one. 0x80 is -0 in fn but NaN in fnuz, so it becomes 0.
    The weight is updated in place. Exponents 254 and 255 cannot be
    bumped and become 0xFF (NaN); real checkpoints never use them.

*vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.mxfp8_utils.requant_block_fp8_to_ue8m0*

requant_block_fp8_to_ue8m0(weight, scale)
    Requantize block-FP8 weights to E4M3 with one UE8M0 scale per 1x32.

    The SM100 MegaMoE feeds its scales to the block-scaled MMA, so they
    have to be powers of two, one per row and 32 columns. A checkpoint
    with float32 scales per block (e.g. 128x128) is rounded once more to
    get there.

    Parameters: ~
        weight (Tensor)
            `(n, mn, k)` E4M3 values.

        scale (Tensor)
            `(n, mn / block_m, k / block_k)` float32 dequantization
            scales (`real = weight * scale`).

    Returns: ~
        Tensor
            `(weight, sf)`: the requantized E4M3 weights and their UE8M0
            scale

        Tensor
            bytes, `(n, mn, k / 32)` uint8.

swizzle_mxfp8_scale(sf, M, K)

*vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.nvfp4_emulation_utils._e2m1_inline*

_e2m1_inline(nibble)
    Decode an NVFP4 nibble (4 bits: 1 sign + 3 magnitude) to float32.

    Uses direct IEEE 754 bit construction. For magnitudes 2-7 the FP32
    bit pattern is 0x3F000000 + (mag << 22), which is a single shift +
    add + bitcast. Magnitudes 0 (zero) and 1 (E2M1 subnormal = 0.5) are
    patched with two tl.where ops.

*vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.nvfp4_emulation_utils._e4m3_inline*

_e4m3_inline(byte)
    Decode an FP8 E4M3FN byte to float32 without an FP8 pointer type.

    Typed FP8 loads need SM89+ in Triton; reading the scale as uint8 and
    decoding here keeps the caller portable.

*vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.nvfp4_emulation_utils._nvfp4_gathered_bias_kernel*

_nvfp4_gathered_bias_kernel(markov_ptr, packed_weight_ptr, weight_scale_ptr,
    global_scale_ptr, values_ptr, index_ptr, logits_ptr, stride_markov_b,
    stride_markov_k, stride_weight_v, stride_weight_k, stride_scale_v,
    stride_scale_k, stride_values_b, stride_values_j, stride_index_b,
    stride_index_j, stride_logits_b, stride_logits_v, alpha, TOPK, K,
    NUM_BLOCKS)
    Apply selected NVFP4 Markov-projection rows to dense logits.

    BF16: `weight[index] -> baddbmm_ -> scatter_`. NVFP4:
    `gather packed W2 row -> dequantize 16-element blocks -> dot with Markov embedding -> add base value -> scatter corrected logit`.

    The fused NVFP4 path is needed because packed weights cannot be
    indexed as BF16 rows, while dequantizing the full vocabulary would
    defeat top-k.

*vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.nvfp4_emulation_utils._nvfp4_quant_dequant_kernel*

_nvfp4_quant_dequant_kernel(input_ptr, output_ptr, global_scale_ptr, k,
    num_blocks, BLOCK_SIZE, FP4_MAX_RECIPROCAL, TILE_BLOCKS)
    Fused NVFP4 quantize-dequantize kernel.

    Uses a 2D grid (rows x tiles) to parallelize across both rows and
    quantization groups within a row. Each program handles TILE_BLOCKS
    groups at once using vectorized 2D operations.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------
                  *vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.ocp_mx_utils*

Functions: ~

*vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.ocp_mx_utils.ocp_mx_weight_dtype_and_rows*

ocp_mx_weight_dtype_and_rows(weight_quant)
    Normalize a Quark weight quant config to
    `(mx_dtype, scale_block_rows)`.

    Quark spells OCP MX weights two ways. The canonical one is 1-D
    per-group: `qscheme="per_group"`, `group_size=32`,
    `scale_format="e8m0"`. MXFP8 checkpoints may instead use a 2-D
    per-block spelling (`qscheme="per_block"`, `block_size=[R, 32]`,
    `scale_type="float8_e8m0fnu"`), which carries one scale per `R`
    weight rows rather than one per row. `scale_block_rows` is that `R`;
    it is 1 for the canonical spelling, where the two layouts coincide.

    Returns `None` when the config is not an OCP MX weight quantization.

    folded into the per-expert dequantization alphas, we can only ensure
    that the quant/dequant scales match by having a single quantization
    scale shared across all ranks.

            *vllm.model_executor.layers.sparse_attn_indexer.SparseAttnIndexer*

SparseAttnIndexer
    Bases: `CustomOp`

    Sparse Attention Indexer Custom Op Layer. This layer is extracted as
    a separate custom op since it involves heavy custom kernels like
    `mqa_logits`, `paged_mqa_logits` and `top_k_per_row`, etc. Those
    kernels maybe requires specific memory layout or implementation for
    different hardware backends to achieve optimal performance.

    For now, the default native path will use CUDA backend path. Other
    platform may requires add the corresponding Custom Op name
    `sparse_attn_indexer` to `custom_ops` in `CompilationConfig` to
    enable the platform specific path.

    Methods: ~

    forward_cpu  CPU sparse attention indexer: cache write stays eager Python
                 glue

    forward_cpu(hidden_states, q_quant, k, weights)
    *vllm.model_executor.layers.sparse_attn_indexer.SparseAttnIndexer.forward_cpu*
        CPU sparse attention indexer: cache write stays eager Python
        glue (own K-cache layout, not shared with the main attention
        cache write). PREFILL and DECODE both call the ported
        `fp8_paged_mqa_logits_cpu`/`topk_transform_512_cpu` kernels,
        which read the paged K-cache directly via `page_table` -- no
        eager gather step, no per-request Python loop.

        `prefill_metadata.chunks` always has exactly one entry here:
        `DeepseekV4CPUIndexerMetadataBuilder` overrides the base chunk
        split to always return the whole step's prefill batch as one
        chunk, since the base chunking only bounds CUDA/XPU's dense M*N
        logits tensor and flat K-gather workspace, neither of which this
        paged kernel allocates.

         *vllm.model_executor.layers.sparse_attn_indexer._decode_chunk_ranges*

     *vllm.model_executor.layers.sparse_attn_indexer._gather_workspace_shapes*

_gather_workspace_shapes(total_seq_lens, head_dim, fp8_dtype, use_fp4_cache)
    Return ((values_shape, values_dtype), (scales_shape, scales_dtype))
    for the K-gather workspace. FP8 path: (T, head_dim) fp8 + (T, 4)
    uint8 fp32 scales. MXFP4 path: (T, head_dim // 2) uint8 packed mxfp4
    + (T, head_dim // MXFP4_BLOCK_SIZE) uint8 ue8m0 scales.

       *vllm.model_executor.layers.sparse_attn_indexer._merge_dcp_topk_global*

_merge_dcp_topk_global(logits, topk_indices, topk_tokens, dcp_rank,
    dcp_world_size, cp_interleave, row_starts=None,
    logits_dtype=torch.float32, num_positions=None, direct_max_rows=0)
    Merge each DCP rank's local top-K into the global top-K.

    `topk_indices` are this rank's local top-K positions into its 1/N KV
    shard. A token in the global top-K must also be in its owning rank's
    local top-K (at most `topk_tokens - 1` tokens rank globally above
    it, hence at most that many on its own rank), so exchanging only the
    per-rank local candidates is exact -- equivalent to all-gathering
    the full logit matrix, but it ships `dcp_world_size * topk_tokens`
    candidates instead of the whole score row. Overwrites `topk_indices`
    with global token ids (`-1` for padding); the attention backend
    localizes them back to physical slots per rank. The selector keys
    only the score bits that `logits_dtype` (the dtype the MQA logits
    were computed in, before the FP32 upcast) carries and the id bits
    that positions below `num_positions` use.

    Batches of at most `direct_max_rows` rows exchange the candidates
    over symmetric memory instead of an NCCL all-gather (the workspace
    was created by `SparseAttnIndexer`).

          *vllm.model_executor.layers.sparse_attn_indexer._varlen_decode_rows*

_varlen_decode_rows(q, q_scale, weights, kv_cache, decode, max_model_len,
    max_seq_len, topk_backend, topk_tokens, topk_indices_buffer,
    candidate_blocks, candidate_block_size, candidate_write, logits_dtype,
    start, end)
    The varlen (SM100) decode logits, candidate selection and top-k of
    rows `[start, end)`, with the slice's own DeepGEMM schedule.

               *vllm.model_executor.layers.sparse_attn_indexer.as_fp32_logits*

as_fp32_logits(logits, row_ends)
    Upcast BF16 MQA logits for the FP32 top-k kernels.

    Only columns below `row_ends` (int32, one per row) are converted,
    the span the consumers read; DeepGEMM's aligned row stride is kept,

----------------------------------------------------------------------------
                               *vllm.model_executor.layers.sparse_mqa_indexer*

Sparse Attention Indexer that scores only the candidate blocks.

DeepSeek V4.1 two-level selection: the candidate-source indexer
publishes the top candidate blocks and later indexers pick their top-k
inside them. `SparseAttnIndexer` does that by computing dense logits
over the whole context and masking; this layer instead calls DeepGEMM's
sparse MQA-logits kernels on the candidate blocks only, so the work is
O(candidate blocks) instead of O(context). It requires the
    `DeepseekV41SparseIndexerBackend` metadata (see
    `AttentionConfig.indexer_sparse_logits`).

Classes: ~

SparseMQAIndexer  Candidate-consuming indexer on DeepGEMM's sparse MQA-logits
                  kernels.

                        *vllm.model_executor.layers.utils._amd_l3_cache_bytes*

_amd_l3_cache_bytes(cache_info=None)
    The GPU's L3 (memory-side) cache size in bytes, or None.

    The skinny-GEMM weight cap tracks this cache: past it a weight
    cannot stay resident, and the skinny kernel's cost at n activation
    rows (~n weight passes) pays HBM round trips instead. The
    device-properties API exposes only the far smaller L2 (4 MiB on
    gfx950), so query the L3 through AMD's amdsmi library: 256 MiB on
    MI355X, 128 MiB on MI300X-class parts. `cache_info` (an amdsmi cache
    list) lets tests drive the parse; the default queries the library.

                   *vllm.model_executor.layers.utils._bf16_mm_shape_supported*

_bf16_mm_shape_supported(x, weight, bias)

    backend.

              *vllm.model_executor.layers.utils._skinny_gemm_max_weight_bytes*

_skinny_gemm_max_weight_bytes() cached
    Effective skinny-GEMM weight cap in bytes, evaluated once.

    VLLM_SKINNY_GEMM_MAX_WEIGHT_BYTES > 0 overrides; 0 (the default)
    derives the cap from the hardware L3 (memory-side) cache size,
    falling back to _SKINNY_GEMM_FALLBACK_WEIGHT_BYTES where that cannot
    be read. lmhead_skinny_guard_permits runs per decode step, so this
    is computed on the first call only (env access in hot paths:
    #17067). Tests that change the env var or mock the hardware read
    must call cache_clear().

                *vllm.model_executor.layers.utils.lmhead_skinny_guard_permits*

lmhead_skinny_guard_permits(weight, n)
    Should this weight still take the wvSplitK skinny path at n?

    wvSplitK_hf_sml's cost at n activation rows scales as ~n passes over
    the weight (MI355X measurements in the PR description), so past the
    last-level (memory-side) cache its effective bandwidth collapses:
    every pass beyond the first is an HBM round trip. Weights above
    VLLM_SKINNY_GEMM_MAX_WEIGHT_BYTES (default: the memory-side cache
    size, read from the hardware once at first use, 256 MiB on MI355X;
    see envs.py for what the cap controls and how to tune it) therefore
    skip the skinny path at 1 < n <= 5 and fall through to the generic
    GEMM.

    n == 1 always keeps wvSplitK: the n=1 kernel variant shows no
    pathology on large weights, and its fall-through would be a numerics
    change with no speed win, so single-row calls stay on the stock
    path.

    Returns True (keep wvSplitK) when n <= 1 or the weight is under the
    cap; otherwise returns False after emitting a census WARNING (once
    per (shape, n) per process) naming the redirected site.

      *vllm.model_executor.layers.utils.maybe_pad_weight_avoid_cache_aliasing*

maybe_pad_weight_avoid_cache_aliasing(weight)
    Offset a dense weight's row stride so it stops aliasing.

    Returns a view with the original shape whose row stride is one cache
    line wider, or `weight` unchanged when the pad does not apply.

                      *vllm.model_executor.layers.utils.maybe_use_skinny_gemm*

         *vllm.model_executor.layers.utils.warmup_rocm_skinny_gemm_workspaces*

warmup_rocm_skinny_gemm_workspaces(device) cached
    Eagerly allocate wvSplitKrc's per-device split-K workspace pool.

    wvSplitKrc partitions one per-device allocation into `kWvSlots`
    slots (csrc/rocm/skinny_gemms_wvsplitkrc.cu) and hands each stream
    one on first use, so that two streams never share the split-K
    partials and counters.

    The pool is otherwise created lazily on the first qualifying GEMM
    (csrc/rocm/skinny_gemms_wvsplitkrc.cu), which can be the first real
    request --- after the KV cache backing buffer exists. If it landed
    in that segment's rounding tail, it would pin the entire segment at
    engine shutdown; it could also land inside a cudagraph capture,
    where it would be taken from the graph's private pool and its
    zero-fill would become a replayed graph node.

                        *vllm.model_executor.layers.utils.wvsplitkrc_dispatch*

wvsplitkrc_dispatch(n, k, m, cu_count)
    Pick the K-shard split for wvSplitKrc and say whether the shape
    fits.

    Mirrors wvSplitKrc() in csrc/rocm/skinny_gemms_wvsplitkrc.cu, which
    is also where the shard cap is explained. Both must pick the same
    chunkk or the workspace check here bounds the wrong k_rnd.

    Returns: ~
        int
            The CHUNKK the kernel will dispatch with, and whether the CU
            budget and

        bool
            split-K workspace admit the shape at all.

  *vllm.model_executor.layers.vocab_parallel_embedding.VocabParallelEmbedding*

VocabParallelEmbedding
    Bases: `PluggableLayer`

    Embedding parallelized in the vocabulary dimension.

    Adapted from torch.nn.Embedding, note that we pad the vocabulary
    size to make sure it is divisible by the number of model parallel
    GPUs.

    In order to support various loading methods, we ensure that
    LoRA-added embeddings are always at the end of TP-sharded tensors.
    In other words, we shard base embeddings and LoRA embeddings
    separately (both padded), and place them in the same tensor. In this
    example, we will have the original vocab size = 1010, added vocab
    size = 16 and padding to 64. Therefore, the total vocab size with
    padding will be 1088 (because we first pad 1010 to 1024, add 16, and
    then pad to 1088). Therefore, the tensor format looks like the
    following: TP1, rank 0 (no sharding): |< --------BASE-------- >|<
    -BASE PADDING-- >|< -----LORA------ >|< -LORA PADDING-- >|
    corresponding token_id: | 0 | 1 | ... | 1009 | -1 | ... | -1 | 1010
    | ... | 1025 | -1 | ... | -1 | index: | 0 | 1 | ... | 1009 | 1010 |
    ... | 1023 | 1024 | ... | 1039 | 1040 | ... | 1087 |

    TP2, rank 0: |< --------------------BASE--------------------- >|<
    -----LORA------ >|< -LORA PADDING- >| corresponding token_id: | 0 |
    1 | 2 | ... | 497 | 498 | ... | 511 | 1010 | ... | 1025 | -1 | ... |
    -1 | index: | 0 | 1 | 2 | ... | 497 | 498 | ... | 511 | 512 | ... |
    527 | 528 | ... | 543 | TP2, rank 1: |< -----------BASE-----------
    >|< -BASE PADDING- >|< -----------LORA PADDING----------- >|
    corresponding token_id: | 512 | 513 | 514 | ... | 1009 | -1 | ... |
    -1 | -1 | ... | -1 | -1 | ... | -1 | index: | 0 | 1 | 2 | ... | 497
    | 498 | ... | 511 | 512 | ... | 527 | 528 | ... | 543 |

    Parameters: ~
        num_embeddings (int)
            vocabulary size.

        embedding_dim (int)
            size of hidden state.

        params_dtype (dtype | None, default: None)
            type of the parameters.

        org_num_embeddings (int | None, default: None)
            original vocabulary size (without LoRA).

        padding_size (int, default: DEFAULT_VOCAB_PADDING_SIZE)
            padding size for the vocabulary.

        quant_config (QuantizationConfig | None, default: None)
            quant config for the layer

        prefix (str, default: '')
            full name of the layer in the state dict

        disable_tp (bool, default: False)
            If true, tensor parallelism will be disabled for this layer.

        reduce_results (bool, default: True)
            Whether to all-reduce contributions from vocabulary shards.

        quant_method (QuantizeMethodBase | None, default: None)
            Preselected quantization method for model-specific layers.

        parallel_group (GroupCoordinator | None, default: None)
            Process group used to shard and reduce the embedding.

    Methods: ~

    forward                      Look up IDs, optionally reducing
                                 contributions from vocabulary shards.
    get_sharded_to_full_mapping  Get a mapping that can be used to reindex the
                                 gathered

    _get_indices(vocab_size_padded, org_vocab_size_padded, vocab_size,
        org_vocab_size, tp_rank, tp_size) classmethod
    *vllm.model_executor.layers.vocab_parallel_embedding.VocabParallelEmbedding._get_indices*
        Get start and end indices for vocab parallel embedding,
        following the layout outlined in the class docstring, based on
        the given tp_rank and tp_size.

    forward(input_)
    *vllm.model_executor.layers.vocab_parallel_embedding.VocabParallelEmbedding.forward*
        Look up IDs, optionally reducing contributions from vocabulary
        shards.

    get_sharded_to_full_mapping()
    *vllm.model_executor.layers.vocab_parallel_embedding.VocabParallelEmbedding.get_sharded_to_full_mapping*
        Get a mapping that can be used to reindex the gathered logits
        for sampling.

        During sampling, we gather logits from all ranks. The
        relationship of index->token_id will follow the same format as
        outlined in the class docstring. However, after the gather, we
        want to reindex the final logits tensor to map index->token_id
        one-to-one (the index is always equal the token_id it
        corresponds to). The indices returned by this method allow us to
        do that.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------
                    *vllm.model_executor.model_loader.checkpoint_weight_patch*

Apply dense or sparse weight updates in checkpoint coordinates.

The model's `load_weights` method still handles checkpoint-name mapping,
TP slicing, and packed parameters. Sparse patches use NaN to mark
unchanged checkpoint elements. The supported sparse-loader contract
permits only final same-shaped floating-point `Tensor.copy_` writes.
Composed, multi-stage, and custom-write loaders are unsupported.

Classes: ~

CheckpointWeightPatch  Describe one dense or sparse checkpoint-coordinate
                       update.

Functions: ~

load_checkpoint_weight_patches  Load ordered patches through the model's
                                checkpoint loader.

*vllm.model_executor.model_loader.checkpoint_weight_patch.CheckpointWeightPatch*

CheckpointWeightPatch
    Bases: `NamedTuple`

    Describe one dense or sparse checkpoint-coordinate update.

    Attributes: ~
        name (str)
            Checkpoint weight name passed to the model loader.

        shape (tuple[int, ...])
            Full checkpoint tensor shape.

        dtype (dtype)
            Checkpoint tensor dtype.

        values (Tensor)
            The flattened full tensor for a dense patch, or the values at
            `indices` for a sparse patch.

        indices (Tensor | None)
            Flat indices into the full checkpoint tensor described by `shape`.
            `None` makes `values` a dense replacement.

*vllm.model_executor.model_loader.checkpoint_weight_patch._load_nan_masked_weights*

_load_nan_masked_weights(model, weights)

    at NaNs.

*vllm.model_executor.model_loader.checkpoint_weight_patch.load_checkpoint_weight_patches*

load_checkpoint_weight_patches(model, patches, *,
    max_chunk_bytes=_DEFAULT_PATCH_CHUNK_BYTES, validate_unique_indices=True)
    Load ordered patches through the model's checkpoint loader.

    A call may contain either dense or sparse patches, but not both. A
    repeated name starts a new loader call, so patches for that weight
    are applied in input order. A later patch may update positions
    changed by an earlier patch. Each sparse patch creates a full
    checkpoint-shaped tensor whose NaNs mark unchanged elements. Each
    locally applied sparse patch must use one final same-shaped
    floating-point `Tensor.copy_`. Intermediate or unrelated `copy_`
    calls, composed loaders, and custom write paths are unsupported.
    `max_chunk_bytes` is a batching target; one tensor may exceed it.

    Online checkpoint-format dense updates require the caller to manage
    vLLM's layerwise reload lifecycle. Sparse online updates modify
    initialized model tensors in place and must not use that lifecycle.
    Patch shapes, dtypes, value lengths, and sparse indices are
    validated before loading begins.

    This function does not roll back a partial update. If a loader fails
    after a write, some destinations may already be changed. Do not
    serve from the affected worker until a known baseline has been
    restored or the worker has been restarted.

    Parameters: ~
        model (Module)
            Model whose native `load_weights` method applies the
            patches.

        patches (Iterable[CheckpointWeightPatch])
            Dense replacements or sparse updates in checkpoint
            coordinates.

        max_chunk_bytes (int, default: _DEFAULT_PATCH_CHUNK_BYTES)
            Target checkpoint tensor bytes per `model.load_weights` call
            and patch bytes per sparse validation batch. A single tensor
            may exceed this target.

        validate_unique_indices (bool, default: True)
            Whether to reject duplicate sparse indices within each
            patch. Repeated patches may update the same positions.
            Disable only for a trusted producer that already guarantees
            unique positions within each patch.

    Returns: ~
        set[str]
            Union of the weight names reported by all
            `model.load_weights` calls.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------
                           *vllm.model_executor.model_loader.ep_weight_filter*

Filter out non-local expert weights during loading to avoid redundant
I/O.

In DP+EP deployments each rank only needs its own expert shard. Skipping
non-local expert tensors before they are read from disk eliminates the
majority of storage I/O for MoE models (experts typically account for
~85-90 % of total weight bytes).

Functions: ~

compute_eplb_local_expert_ids  Compute the logical expert ids ep_rank must
                               load when EPLB is on.
compute_local_expert_ids       Compute the set of global expert ids owned by
                               ep_rank.
parse_expert_id                Return the expert id embedded in weight_name,
                               or `None` if it is
should_skip_weight             Return `True` if weight_name is an expert
                               weight that does not

*vllm.model_executor.model_loader.ep_weight_filter.compute_eplb_local_expert_ids*

compute_eplb_local_expert_ids(num_experts, num_redundant_experts, ep_size,
    ep_rank)
    Compute the logical expert ids ep_rank must load when EPLB is on.

    EPLB splits `num_experts + num_redundant_experts` physical slots
    linearly across ranks and fills each from the initial
    physical-to-logical map, so redundant slots can need experts from
    other ranks' shards. Rebalancing later moves weights GPU-to-GPU, so
    loading only has to satisfy the initial map.

    Returns `None` when EP is not active (`ep_size <= 1`).

  *vllm.model_executor.model_loader.ep_weight_filter.compute_local_expert_ids*

compute_local_expert_ids(num_experts, ep_size, ep_rank, placement='linear')
    Compute the set of global expert ids owned by ep_rank.

    Returns `None` when EP is not active (`ep_size <= 1`), meaning all
    experts are local and no filtering should be performed.

    The distribution logic mirrors
    `vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.layer.determine_expert_map`.

    Parameters: ~
        num_experts (int)
            Total number of experts in the layer.

        ep_size (int)
            Expert parallel world size.

        ep_rank (int)
            Rank whose local expert ids are computed.

        placement (str, default: 'linear')
            `"linear"` for contiguous assignment, `"round_robin"` for
            interleaved assignment.

           *vllm.model_executor.model_loader.ep_weight_filter.parse_expert_id*

parse_expert_id(weight_name)
    Return the expert id embedded in weight_name, or `None` if it is not
    an per-expert weight.

    Returns `None` for dense weights (attention, layernorm, embedding),
    shared experts, and 3D fused-expert tensors where all experts are
    stored in a single tensor without a numeric expert id in the name.

        *vllm.model_executor.model_loader.ep_weight_filter.should_skip_weight*

should_skip_weight(weight_name, local_expert_ids)
    Return `True` if weight_name is an expert weight that does not
    belong to the local rank and should be skipped during loading.

                             *vllm.model_executor.model_loader.IpcModelLoader*

IpcModelLoader
    Bases: `BaseModelLoader`

    Zero-copy loads a model using the weight cache daemon's sharing
    backend.

    The model is initialized on the meta device and every
    parameter/buffer is replaced by the daemon's post-quantized tensor,
    so process_weights_after_loading is skipped entirely. The engine
    shares the daemon's GPU memory.

    Extra config keys (via --model-loader-extra-config):

    - socket_path: explicit daemon socket path. Defaults to a per-GPU
      path derived from the physical GPU uuid and the cache role
      (target/draft).
    - socket_dir: directory containing the daemon sockets.
    - fallback: fall back to disk loading when fetching state fails
      because the daemon is unavailable or the fingerprints mismatch
      (default: True).
    - connect_timeout_s: socket connect timeout (default: 5.0).
    - state_timeout_s: timeout for the weight-transfer request (default:
      300.0).

    The weights live in externally held backend allocations, so sleep
    mode (CuMemAllocator weight offloading) must not be used with this
    loader. If the daemon exits, the CUDA driver keeps the mapped
    weights alive until the engine exits, so the engine keeps serving;
    the loader watches the daemon and warns since a restarted daemon
    then holds a second copy of the weights on the GPU.

    _rebuild_storages(state)
    *vllm.model_executor.model_loader.IpcModelLoader._rebuild_storages*
        Rebuild manifest tensors from one imported buffer per storage.

    _watch_daemon()
    *vllm.model_executor.model_loader.IpcModelLoader._watch_daemon*
        Watch for the exit of the daemon serving the zero-copy weights.

        The daemon holds the watch connection open for its lifetime, so
        the connection closes exactly when that daemon instance exits; a
        daemon restarted on the same socket does not mask the loss.

    _with_startup_wait(op)
    *vllm.model_executor.model_loader.IpcModelLoader._with_startup_wait*
        Retry op until the daemon answers or the state timeout elapses;
        the daemon may still be loading the model when the engine
        starts.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------
                                     *vllm.model_executor.model_loader.reload*

Layerwise weight reloading utilities for vLLM.

This module provides functionality to reload model weights
layer-by-layer, which is useful for weight updates without full model
reconstruction.

Limitations: 1. Composition with CPU offloading has not been implemented
2. Tied parameters will only reflect processing from one of the parent
layers (for example, only processing from embed_tokens will have an
effect) 3. This design assumes that the number of weights loaded from
disk is the same as the number of weights created at model init time.
This is not true for quant methods which (1) pad weights or (2) load qkv
weights into the same parameter. Both of these cases are non-issues for
today's quant methods, but future quantizations may cause reloading to
fail

Modules: ~

bake       The load plan's bake: run `load_weights` once over `TraceTensor`s,
           on
direct     Direct weight reload (`VLLM_RELOAD_MODE=direct`, or `auto` where it
           applies).
geometry   Integer geometry of the load plan: one traced `copy_` as a box of
           the
inplace
layerwise
lifecycle  Begin and complete a checkpoint-format weight update in the reload
           mode
meta
plan       Load plan: which part of each checkpoint tensor this rank needs,
           and where
sanitize
trace      Tracing a model's weight loaders on zero-storage checkpoint
           tensors.
utils

                            *vllm.model_executor.model_loader.reload.LoadPlan*

LoadPlan dataclass
    Methods: ~

    get_boxes  Parts of the checkpoint tensor this rank needs; `None`:
               nothing.
    get_dest   (part of a box, live tensor) pairs: copying each part, reshaped
               to

    get_boxes(name)
    *vllm.model_executor.model_loader.reload.LoadPlan.get_boxes*
        Parts of the checkpoint tensor this rank needs; `None`: nothing.

        For engines that send or read only those slices (sharded RDT,
        NCCL M2N follow-ups); an engine that receives full tensors calls
        `load_planned` instead.

    get_dest(name)
    *vllm.model_executor.model_loader.reload.LoadPlan.get_dest*
        (part of a box, live tensor) pairs: copying each part, reshaped
        to its tensor's shape, into that tensor is exactly what the
        loader would have written. `None`: fallback, send the full
        tensor through `load_weights`. Write only between `start_reload`
        and `finish_reload`; never read. A tensor may be in another
        dtype than the checkpoint tensor, so write it with `copy_`, not
        as raw bytes.

        `load_planned` copies full tensors through it; an engine that
        sends only `get_boxes` copies its slices the same way.

                     *vllm.model_executor.model_loader.reload.check_plannable*

check_plannable(model)
    Refuse a configuration no load plan supports: a reload mode other
    than direct, EPLB, and online quantization (its loaders quantize
    what they load). Reads only configuration, so an engine can call it
    before `start_reload` changes the model. Direct reload's own
    refusals run in `begin_direct_reload`.

    Raises: ~
        RuntimeError
            the configuration cannot be planned.

       *vllm.model_executor.model_loader.reload.finalize_layerwise_processing*

finalize_layerwise_processing(model, model_config)
    Apply processing to any layers which were not layerwise processed
    during loading. This includes attention layers and layers which have
    weight elements which are not loaded (due to padding).

    This function should be applied after `initialize_layerwise_reload`
    is applied unwrap the layerwise weight loaders.

    Parameters: ~
        model (Module)
            model to finalize processing for

        model_config (ModelConfig)
            config needed for applying processing to attention layers

                       *vllm.model_executor.model_loader.reload.finish_reload*

finish_reload(model, model_config, device)
    Complete the weight update `start_reload` began.

         *vllm.model_executor.model_loader.reload.initialize_layerwise_reload*

initialize_layerwise_reload(model, *, defer_processing=False)
    Set up layerwise weight loading with deferred processing.

    Must be called after `record_metadata_for_reloading`. This function:
    1. Saves current kernel tensors for later copying 2. Restores layer
    parameters/buffers from metadata (on meta device) 3. Wraps weight
    loaders to defer processing until all weights are loaded

    When all weights for a layer are loaded, the wrapped loaders will:
    1. Materialize the layer onto the target device 2. Load all cached
    weights 3. Run quantization processing if applicable 4. Copy
    processed values back to original tensor storage

    With defer_processing=True, only finalize_layerwise_reload triggers
    processing.

                        *vllm.model_executor.model_loader.reload.load_planned*

load_planned(model, plan, weights)
    Load full checkpoint tensors as `plan` says: copy each direct name's
    boxes into its destinations, skip names this rank needs nothing of,
    and pass fallbacks to `model.load_weights`. Call between
    `start_reload` and `finish_reload`.

    Copies are batched, so each tensor `weights` yields must stay
    unchanged until this call returns: do not reuse one buffer across
    items.

                          *vllm.model_executor.model_loader.reload.plan_loads*

plan_loads(model, metadata)
    Trace `model.load_weights` over the declared checkpoint tensors once
    and return where each lands on this rank.

    Call between `start_reload` and `finish_reload`: the plan traces the
    real tensors in the layout `begin_direct_reload` applied. Incoming
    tensors are data-free traces, so nothing is loaded. Loaders'
    constant writes land, as on the `load_weights` path; so do writes
    into non-checkpoint GPU tensors fed by a read of a checkpoint tensor
    (a mirror), which are not restored: that name falls back and the
    update rewrites them. Module, parameter and buffer state a loader
    sets stays, as it would after `load_weights`.

    Raises: ~
        ValueError
            a name is declared twice.

        RuntimeError
            the model cannot be planned.

       *vllm.model_executor.model_loader.reload.record_metadata_for_reloading*

record_metadata_for_reloading(model)
    Record layer metadata needed for later reloading.

    Stores parameter and buffer metadata as meta tensors for
    restoration. Must be called before `initialize_layerwise_reload`.

                        *vllm.model_executor.model_loader.reload.start_reload*

start_reload(model)
    Begin a weight update in the configured mode.

                *vllm.model_executor.model_loader.reload.weight_update_active*

weight_update_active()

    hold only part of the checkpoint. Process-wide, so a module nested
    in the model passed to `start_reload` sees it too.

                *vllm.model_executor.model_loader.tensorizer.TensorizerConfig*

TensorizerConfig dataclass
    Bases: `MutableMapping`

    _keys class-attribute
    *vllm.model_executor.model_loader.tensorizer.TensorizerConfig._keys*
        Configuration class for Tensorizer settings.

        These settings configure the behavior of model serialization and
        deserialization using Tensorizer.

        Attributes: ~
            tensorizer_uri
                Path to serialized model tensors. Can be a local file path or
                a S3 URI. Unless a `tensorizer_dir` is passed to this object's
                initializer, this is a required argument.

            tensorizer_dir
                Path to a directory containing serialized model tensors, and
                all other potential model artifacts to load the model, such as
                configs and tokenizer files. Can be passed instead of
                `tensorizer_uri` where the `model.tensors` file will be
                assumed to be in this directory.

            vllm_tensorized
                If True, indicates that the serialized model is a vLLM model.
                This is used to determine the behavior of the
                TensorDeserializer when loading tensors from a serialized
                model. It is far faster to deserialize a vLLM model as it
                utilizes tensorizer's optimized GPU loading. Note that this is
                now deprecated, as serialized vLLM models are now
                automatically inferred as vLLM models.

            verify_hash
                If True, the hashes of each tensor will be verified against
                the hashes stored in the metadata. A `HashMismatchError` will
                be raised if any of the hashes do not match.

            num_readers
                Controls how many threads are allowed to read concurrently
                from the source file. Default is `None`, which will
                dynamically set the number of readers based on the number of
                available resources and model size. This greatly increases
                performance.

            encryption_keyfile
                File path to a binary file containing a binary key to use for
                decryption. `None` (the default) means no decryption. See the
                example script in examples/features/tensorize_vllm_model.py.

            s3_access_key_id
                The access key for the S3 bucket. Can also be set via the
                S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID environment variable.

            s3_secret_access_key
                The secret access key for the S3 bucket. Can also be set via
                the S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY environment variable.

            s3_endpoint
                The endpoint for the S3 bucket. Can also be set via the
                S3_ENDPOINT_URL environment variable.

              *vllm.model_executor.model_loader.tensorizer.is_vllm_tensorized*

is_vllm_tensorized(tensorizer_config)

----------------------------------------------------------------------------
                        *vllm.model_executor.model_loader.weight_cache.daemon*

Weight cache daemon for fast engine restarts.

One daemon process per GPU holds the post-quantized, TP-sharded weights
of its rank in GPU memory and serves shared storage handles to vLLM
engines over a Unix domain socket. Restarting engines map the weights
zero-copy instead of reloading from disk.

Launch one daemon per TP rank with a single command:

>text
    vllm preload \
        --model /path/to/model --tensor-parallel-size 4
<
Engines then load from the daemons with:

>text
    vllm serve /path/to/model --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
        --load-format ipc_cache
<
Tensor, expert, data and pipeline parallelism are supported.

For multi-node tensor parallelism, run one launcher per node with a
shared rendezvous so the global TP group forms across nodes (weight
sharing is node-local, so each node serves only its local GPUs' shards).
Reuse the same `--nnodes`/`--node-rank`/`--master-addr` flags you pass
the engine, plus a `--weight-cache-master-port` distinct from the
engine's `--master-port`:

>text
    # node 0 (8 local GPUs)
    vllm preload \
        --model /path/to/model --tensor-parallel-size 16 \
        --nnodes 2 --node-rank 0 --master-addr 10.0.0.1 \
        --weight-cache-master-port 29600
    # node 1 (8 local GPUs)
    vllm preload \
        --model /path/to/model --tensor-parallel-size 16 \
        --nnodes 2 --node-rank 1 --master-addr 10.0.0.1 \
        --weight-cache-master-port 29600
<
The global TP rank of local GPU `i` on node `r` is
`r * (tp_size // nnodes) + i`, matching vLLM's contiguous per-node rank
assignment, so each engine worker maps its shard from the daemon on its
own node. With pipeline parallelism each node additionally runs one
daemon per PP stage; the global rank is `pp_rank * tp_size + tp_rank`.

For data parallelism (e.g. a TP1 x DP16 x EP decode fleet) run one
launcher per node with the engine's DP placement flags. Local GPU `i`
serves DP rank `start_rank + i // tp_size` and TP rank `i % tp_size`,
and all `dp_size * tp_size` daemons form one world group on
`--data-parallel-address`/`--weight-cache-master-port` so the expert
shards are laid out exactly as in the engine:

>text
    # node r (4 local GPUs)
    vllm preload \
        --model /path/to/model --tensor-parallel-size 1 --enable-expert-parallel \
        --data-parallel-size 16 --data-parallel-size-local 4 \
        --data-parallel-start-rank 4r --data-parallel-address 10.0.0.1 \
        --weight-cache-master-port 29600
<
Data parallelism also combines with multi-node tensor parallelism: pass
both flag sets (`--nnodes`/`--node-rank`/`--master-addr` and the DP
flags with a reachable `--data-parallel-address`). Each node then serves
a contiguous block of the `dp_size * tp_size` global ranks, e.g. TP8 x
DP2 on 4 nodes:

>text
    # node r (4 local GPUs)
    vllm preload \
        --model /path/to/model --tensor-parallel-size 8 --enable-expert-parallel \
        --nnodes 4 --node-rank r --master-addr 10.0.0.1 \
        --data-parallel-size 2 --data-parallel-address 10.0.0.1 \
        --weight-cache-master-port 29600
<
With MTP, EAGLE or EAGLE3 speculative decoding the launcher additionally
starts a draft daemon group that caches the draft model. It uses its own
cache key, Unix sockets (`*_draft.sock`) and rendezvous port
(`--weight-cache-draft-master-port`, default
`--weight-cache-master-port + 1`), so each process serves exactly one
model role. Other draft types are not cached and keep loading from disk
in the engine. With pipeline parallelism only the draft daemons of the
last stage serve the draft model.

*vllm.model_executor.model_loader.weight_cache.daemon--seeding-a-replica-from-another*
SEEDING A REPLICA FROM ANOTHER

with `--weight-cache-seed`; see `docs/features/preload.md`.

    _acquire_gpu_lock(socket_path)
    *vllm.model_executor.model_loader.weight_cache.daemon.WeightCacheDaemon._acquire_gpu_lock*
        Take an exclusive lock guarding this GPU's socket path.

        The lock is advisory and released automatically when the daemon
        exits (or crashes), so a stale socket is only ever removed by
        whoever owns the lock. A running daemon holding it makes a
        second daemon fail fast instead of clobbering the live socket.

    _export_state()
    *vllm.model_executor.model_loader.weight_cache.daemon.WeightCacheDaemon._export_state*
        Export this rank's storage handles, manifest, aliases and flags.

    _handle_watch(conn)
    *vllm.model_executor.model_loader.weight_cache.daemon.WeightCacheDaemon._handle_watch*
        Hold the connection open until this daemon exits.

        Zero-copy engines keep serving from the mapped weights after the
        daemon exits; the closed connection tells them their daemon is
        gone.

    _prune_watchers()
    *vllm.model_executor.model_loader.weight_cache.daemon.WeightCacheDaemon._prune_watchers*
        Close the watch connections of engines that have exited.

    capture_state()
    *vllm.model_executor.model_loader.weight_cache.daemon.WeightCacheDaemon.capture_state*
        Materialize canonical post-warmup storages and drop the model.

    get_model()
    *vllm.model_executor.model_loader.weight_cache.daemon.WeightCacheDaemon.get_model*
        Load the daemon's model, composed from the configured loader.

        Runs the quantization check after model creation but before the
        slow weight load, so an unsupported method fails fast. Online
        quantization always fails the check, so load_model's finalize
        step for it is unnecessary here.

    release_distributed()
    *vllm.model_executor.model_loader.weight_cache.daemon.WeightCacheDaemon.release_distributed*
        Release process groups and BLAS workspaces after loading and
        warmup.

        Serving only exports shared storage handles, so the
        communicators (NCCL, custom all-reduce and FlashInfer
        workspaces) and cached BLAS scratch would otherwise pin GPU
        memory for the daemon's lifetime.

    serve_forever(ready_callback=None)
    *vllm.model_executor.model_loader.weight_cache.daemon.WeightCacheDaemon.serve_forever*
        Serve requests until terminated.

        The socket is only bound once the model is fully cached, so
        clients get a connection error (and fall back to disk) until the
        daemon is ready.

        Parameters: ~
            ready_callback (Callable[[], None] | None, default: None)
                Invoked once the socket is bound and listening, so the
                launcher can report overall readiness.

       *vllm.model_executor.model_loader.weight_cache.daemon.plan_local_ranks*

plan_local_ranks(parallel_config)
    `(local_rank, dp_rank, pp_rank, tp_rank)` for every local daemon.

    Global ranks enumerate DP, PP, then TP:
    `global = dp_rank * pp_size * tp_size + pp_rank * tp_size + tp_rank`.
    With `--nnodes` the engine hands each node a contiguous block of
    global ranks, so node `r` serves `node_rank * local + i`; without it
    a launcher's block starts at `--data-parallel-start-rank * tp_size`.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------
                    *vllm.model_executor.model_loader.weight_cache.ipc_loader*

Map post-processed weights from a local daemon's pluggable sharing

Classes: ~

IpcModelLoader  Zero-copy loads a model using the weight cache daemon's
                sharing backend.

     *vllm.model_executor.model_loader.weight_cache.ipc_loader.IpcModelLoader*

IpcModelLoader
    Bases: `BaseModelLoader`

    Zero-copy loads a model using the weight cache daemon's sharing
    backend.

    The model is initialized on the meta device and every
    parameter/buffer is replaced by the daemon's post-quantized tensor,
    so process_weights_after_loading is skipped entirely. The engine
    shares the daemon's GPU memory.

    Extra config keys (via --model-loader-extra-config):

    - socket_path: explicit daemon socket path. Defaults to a per-GPU
      path derived from the physical GPU uuid and the cache role
      (target/draft).
    - socket_dir: directory containing the daemon sockets.
    - fallback: fall back to disk loading when fetching state fails
      because the daemon is unavailable or the fingerprints mismatch
      (default: True).
    - connect_timeout_s: socket connect timeout (default: 5.0).
    - state_timeout_s: timeout for the weight-transfer request (default:
      300.0).

    The weights live in externally held backend allocations, so sleep
    mode (CuMemAllocator weight offloading) must not be used with this
    loader. If the daemon exits, the CUDA driver keeps the mapped
    weights alive until the engine exits, so the engine keeps serving;
    the loader watches the daemon and warns since a restarted daemon
    then holds a second copy of the weights on the GPU.

    _rebuild_storages(state)
    *vllm.model_executor.model_loader.weight_cache.ipc_loader.IpcModelLoader._rebuild_storages*
        Rebuild manifest tensors from one imported buffer per storage.

    _watch_daemon()
    *vllm.model_executor.model_loader.weight_cache.ipc_loader.IpcModelLoader._watch_daemon*
        Watch for the exit of the daemon serving the zero-copy weights.

        The daemon holds the watch connection open for its lifetime, so
        the connection closes exactly when that daemon instance exits; a
        daemon restarted on the same socket does not mask the loss.

    _with_startup_wait(op)
    *vllm.model_executor.model_loader.weight_cache.ipc_loader.IpcModelLoader._with_startup_wait*
        Retry op until the daemon answers or the state timeout elapses;
        the daemon may still be loading the model when the engine
        starts.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------
                      *vllm.model_executor.model_loader.weight_cache.protocol*

WeightCacheKey fingerprinting and socket protocol for the weight cache
daemon.

The protocol uses pickle over a Unix domain socket and is only intended
for communication between trusted local processes owned by the same
user. The sockets live in a per-user private directory (mode 0700) and
the daemon restricts the socket file permissions to the owner (0600).
Both the daemon and the engine verify that the directory and socket are
owned by the current user and are not group/world accessible before
trusting them, so a different local user cannot pre-plant a malicious
socket at a predictable path.

Classes: ~

                                match the engine.

                                CUDA IPC handles.

                                verified for IPC weight sharing.

                                get_state response.

                                reachable or usable.

                                  cannot serve (platform, EPLB, role).

*vllm.model_executor.model_loader.weight_cache.protocol.check_weight_cache_loader_support*

check_weight_cache_loader_support(vllm_config, model_config, *, is_draft)

----------------------------------------------------------------------------
                     *vllm.model_executor.model_loader.weight_cache.transport*

Daemon-to-daemon seeding over authenticated JSON/TCP or local pickle.

A `Seedable` is one kind of state a daemon can seed to or from a peer
daemon, including warmup caches and weight shards. The target names what
it wants by kind and key fields; the source resolves the key to a
payload; the target validates and installs it:

>text
    request:  {"kind": "flashinfer_autotune", <key fields>..., "token": "..."}
    response: {"status": "ok", "payload": <kind-specific>}
              {"status": "miss"} | {"status": "error", "message": "..."}
<
Remote payloads are JSON values. Large binary state (weights) must not
be inlined: the payload then describes the transfer (e.g. a storage
manifest), and the caller drives the data plane itself.

The TCP connection is unencrypted beyond the shared token; keep the
listener on a trusted network.

Classes: ~

SeedConfig     A daemon's D2D endpoints and shared token (Unix paths need
               none).
SeedTransport  The daemon's D2D seeding endpoint: serves and fetches
               seedables.
Seedable       One kind of state that can flow between peer daemons, both
               ways.

          *vllm.model_executor.model_loader.weight_cache.transport.SeedConfig*

    Bases: `NamedTuple`

    A daemon's D2D endpoints and shared token (Unix paths need none).

       *vllm.model_executor.model_loader.weight_cache.transport.SeedTransport*

                    daemon.

                    raise.

                    validate_remote.
    request         Send one request to the source daemon; None with a log
                    line on failure.

                    unconfigured.

  *vllm.model_executor.model_loader.weight_cache.utils.build_weight_cache_key*

build_weight_cache_key(vllm_config, model_config, *, is_draft=False)
    Fingerprint this rank's shard exactly as `WeightCacheDaemon` does.

    Shared with the daemon so the peer loader requests the shard its own
    daemon fingerprinted: TP/PP ranks come from the rank the daemon (or
    engine worker) stamped on `parallel_config.rank`, and the DP
    placement follows the engine's per-worker view. Draft models always
    use a single pipeline stage.

         *vllm.model_executor.model_loader.weight_cache.utils.collect_tensors*

collect_tensors(model)
    Collect a model's tensors, preserving tied-parameter aliases.

    `named_parameters`/`named_buffers` are iterated with
    `remove_duplicate=False` so tied weights (e.g. `lm_head.weight`
    sharing storage with `embed_tokens.weight`) are not silently
    dropped. Each unique tensor is kept once; every additional name that
    refers to the same tensor object is recorded in the returned alias
    map so the client can re-establish the shared identity instead of
    allocating uninitialized memory for it.

    Returns: ~
        dict[str, Tensor]
            A `(tensors, kinds, aliases)` triple: `tensors` maps a
            canonical

        dict[str, TensorKind]
            name to its tensor, `kinds` maps it to "param" or "buffer",
            and

        dict[str, str]
            `aliases` maps each duplicate name to its canonical name.

   *vllm.model_executor.model_loader.weight_cache.utils.exported_weight_bytes*

exported_weight_bytes(storages)
    Allocation bytes of unique non-CPU storages mapped from cached
    state.

    This is the memory the engine would otherwise allocate for the
    weights itself. `memory_allocated()` also counts daemon-only state
    the engine never maps (communication buffers, warmup workspaces,
    tensors outside parameters/buffers that the engine rebuilds itself),
    so reporting it would shrink the engine's KV cache below that of a
    disk load.

      *vllm.model_executor.model_loader.weight_cache.utils.format_daemon_role*

get_engine_dp_placement(vllm_config, dp_rank)
    `(dp_size, dp_rank)` as the engine fingerprints this DP rank.

    The engine runs the DP ranks of a non-MoE target as independent DP=1

----------------------------------------------------------------------------
                               *vllm.model_executor.model_loader.weight_tying*

Reconcile word embedding tying with what the checkpoint actually
contains.

Functions: ~

maybe_retie_word_embeddings  Re-tie word embeddings that

           *vllm.model_executor.model_loader.weight_tying._get_untied_lm_head*

_get_untied_lm_head(model)
    Locate an `lm_head` that could be tied to the input embeddings.

    Returns `None` unless the model has exactly one of each, so that
    models with several heads (such as MTP) or with already tied weights
    are left alone. Both are found by type rather than by name, because
    `get_input_embeddings` takes different arguments on multimodal
    models and the `lm_head` of a multimodal model is nested inside its
    language model.

    A quantized `lm_head` is also left alone. Its weights may be packed
    under another name, and online quantization creates them after
    loading, so neither their contents nor whether they were loaded can
    be established here. Note that this is a property of the layer, not
    of the model: most quantized models leave the `lm_head` and the
    input embeddings unquantized.

   *vllm.model_executor.model_loader.weight_tying.maybe_retie_word_embeddings*

maybe_retie_word_embeddings(model, model_config)
    Re-tie word embeddings that
    |vllm.config.ModelConfig.maybe_untie_word_embeddings| untied, if the
    loaded `lm_head` turned out to be identical to the input embeddings
    after all.

    Checkpoints produced by quantization or fine-tuning tooling often
    keep a redundant copy of the tied `lm_head`. Sharing the storage
    again reclaims the memory it would otherwise cost.

    Runs once per model: a direct reload reruns post-load processing on
    the cold-started model and must keep its tying. Re-tying there would
    make `lm_head` the input embeddings, and every later update's
    `lm_head` would be dropped.

        *vllm.model_executor.model_loader.weight_utils._fill_random_fp8_codes*

_fill_random_fp8_codes(param, generator)
    Fill an 8-bit float tensor with random finite codes across its
    range.

    Real checkpoints scale FP8 weights to use the whole range, and the
    bit activity of the operands sets GEMM power draw: values from a
    narrow range (few exponent codes) let power-capped GPUs run
    measurably faster than real weights do.
