resolve_visual_encoder_outputs(encoder_outputs, post_layer_norm, *,
    select_layers=None, max_possible_layers=None, last_hs_proc=None,
    feature_select_strategy=None)
    Given the outputs a visual encoder module that may correspond to the
    output of the last layer, or a list of hidden states to be stacked,
    handle post normalization and resolve it into a single output
    tensor.

    Parameters: ~
        encoder_outputs (Tensor | list[Tensor])
            Output of encoder's last layer or all hidden states.

        post_layer_norm (LayerNorm | None)
            Post norm to apply to the output of the encoder.

        select_layers (list[int] | None, default: None)
            Optional layer indices to grab from the encoder outputs; if
            provided, encoder outputs must be a list.

        max_possible_layers (int | None, default: None)
            Total layers in the fully loaded visual encoder.

        last_hs_proc (Callable[[Tensor], Tensor] | None, default: None)
            Optional callable to be applied to the last layer if it is
            used, e.g., pooling head for Siglip. This is done prior to
            feature selection and layer normalization. If select_layers
            are provided, the output of last_hs_proc must be able to be
            concatenated with the other select_layers along the last
            dimension.

        feature_select_strategy (VisionFeatureSelectStrategy | None,
        default: None)
            Defines how to select the hidden states from each layer.

            have different dimension to do ViT. "rope_3d" for 3D rope
            (e.g., Qwen2.5-VL) "rope_2d" for 2D rope (e.g., Kimi-VL)

          tp_size = 2

VoyageQwen3BidirectionalEmbedModel
    Bases: `Module`, `SupportsLoRA`

    Qwen3Model + Voyage embedding head + bidirectional attention.

    Checkpoint conventions (HF): - MLP: gate_proj + up_proj (unfused) -
    Attn: q_proj + k_proj + v_proj (unfused) - Linear head:
    linear.weight - Weights prefixed with "model." (e.g.,
    model.layers.0...)

      vLLM Qwen3Model expects: ~

      - mlp.gate_up_proj (fused)
      - self_attn.qkv_proj (fused)
      - No "model." prefix

             *vllm.model_executor.models.whisper._create_fake_bias_for_k_proj*

_create_fake_bias_for_k_proj(weights, fake_bias_key_name, out_features=None)
    Create full zeros bias for k_proj weight in self-attn and x-attn
    layers. So that the bias for k_proj in qkv_proj or kv_proj can be
    initialized with zeros.

    If the checkpoint already provides a real `.bias` entry for the
    given weight, it is forwarded as-is and no fake bias is injected for
    that layer.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------
                                           *vllm.model_executor.models.zamba2*

PyTorch Zamba2 model implementation for vLLM.

This module implements the Zamba2 architecture from
https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.15242, which combines Mamba and Transformer
architectures in a hybrid model optimized for efficient sequence
modeling. The model alternates between state space model layers and
attention-based layers.

Classes: ~

Zamba2Attention              Multi-head attention mechanism for the Zamba2
                             model.
Zamba2AttentionDecoderLayer  Single decoder layer combining attention and
                             feed-forward networks.
Zamba2ForCausalLM            Zamba2 model with causal language modeling head.
Zamba2HybridLayer            Hybrid layer combining Transformer and Mamba
                             architectures.
Zamba2LoRA                   LoRA layer for the Zamba2 model.
Zamba2MLP                    Feed-forward MLP layer for the Zamba2 model.
Zamba2MambaDecoderLayer      Single Mamba decoder layer with normalization.
Zamba2Model                  Core Zamba2 model combining transformer and Mamba
                             architectures.

                         *vllm.model_executor.models.zamba2.Zamba2HybridLayer*

Zamba2HybridLayer
    Bases: `Module`

    Hybrid layer combining Transformer and Mamba architectures.

    This layer implements the hybrid architecture described in the Zamba
    paper, where a shared transformer pathway processes input in
    parallel with a Mamba pathway. The transformer output is projected
    and added to the Mamba input for enhanced representation learning.

    Methods: ~

    __init__  Initialize the hybrid layer.
    forward   Forward pass through the hybrid layer.

    __init__(shared_transformer, config, block_idx, model_config=None,
        cache_config=None, quant_config=None, prefix='')
    *vllm.model_executor.models.zamba2.Zamba2HybridLayer.__init__*
        Initialize the hybrid layer.

        Parameters: ~
            shared_transformer (Zamba2AttentionDecoderLayer)
                Transformer decoder layer for attention pathway

            config (Zamba2Config)
                The Zamba2 model configuration

            block_idx (int)
                Index of this hybrid block in the model

            model_config (ModelConfig | None, default: None)
                The model config, when available

            cache_config (CacheConfig | None, default: None)
                The KV cache config, when available

            quant_config (QuantizationConfig | None, default: None)
                Configuration for model quantization

            prefix (str, default: '')
                Module prefix used for quantization config lookup

    forward(hidden_states, original_hidden_states, positions)
    *vllm.model_executor.models.zamba2.Zamba2HybridLayer.forward*
        Forward pass through the hybrid layer.

        Processes input through parallel transformer and Mamba paths: 1.
        Transformer path processes input with attention 2. Transformer
        output is projected to match hidden size 3. Projected output is
        added to Mamba path input 4. Final output combines both paths'
        representations

        Parameters: ~
            hidden_states (Tensor)
                Input tensor [batch_size, seq_len, hidden_size]

            original_hidden_states (Tensor)
                Original input for transformer residual connection

            positions (Tensor)
                Position IDs for positional embeddings

        Returns: ~
            Tensor
                Output tensor combining transformer and Mamba
                representations

                             *vllm.model_executor.offloader.PrefetchOffloader*

PrefetchOffloader
    Bases: `BaseOffloader`

    Prefetching-based offloader with group-based layer selection.

    Groups layers and uses async H2D prefetch to hide transfer latency.
    Uses static buffers and stream synchronization for torch.compile and
    CUDA graph compatibility.

    Parameters: ~
        group_size (int)
            Group every N layers together.

        num_in_group (int)

        prefetch_step (int)

        mode (str, default: 'cpu')
            Offload mode ("cpu" is currently supported).

    Methods: ~

    join_after_forward  Join copy_stream after model forward completes.
    post_init           Allocate static buffer pool and start initial
                        prefetches.
    sync_prev_onload    Sync previous onload operations.
    wrap_modules        Wrap modules with prefetch offloading logic.

    _hook_module_forward(index, module)
    *vllm.model_executor.offloader.PrefetchOffloader._hook_module_forward*
        Hook module's forward with torch.compile-compatible sync.

    _start_prefetch(layer_idx)
    *vllm.model_executor.offloader.PrefetchOffloader._start_prefetch*
        Called by custom op - start async copy to static buffer.

    _wait_for_layer(layer_idx)
    *vllm.model_executor.offloader.PrefetchOffloader._wait_for_layer*
        Called by custom op - wait for copy to complete.

        Synchronization strategy: - During CUDA graph capture: use
        event-based wait (graph-compatible) - Outside capture
        (warmup/eager): use wait_stream (more robust)

        During capture, we skip wait for pre-capture prefetches because:
        1. sync_before_graph_capture() ensures pre-capture work is
        complete 2. We can't wait on pre-capture events during capture
        (isolation error)

    join_after_forward()
    *vllm.model_executor.offloader.PrefetchOffloader.join_after_forward*
        Join copy_stream after model forward completes.

        Call this after the model forward pass but before CUDA graph
        capture ends. This ensures copy_stream is rejoined for any
        prefetches started during the forward pass.

        We join ALL layers that have _prefetch_in_capture=True, meaning
        their prefetch was started during capture but not yet waited on
        (joined). This handles both full and piecewise cudagraph modes
        correctly: - Full mode: joins layers 0..prefetch_step-1
        (prefetched by last layers) - Piecewise mode: joins only layers
        prefetched by THIS subgraph's layers

    post_init()
    *vllm.model_executor.offloader.PrefetchOffloader.post_init*
        Allocate static buffer pool and start initial prefetches.

        Note: Parameters have already been offloaded to CPU during
        wrap_modules() (in _CpuParamOffloader.init), so GPU memory is
        available for the static buffer pool.

    sync_prev_onload()
    *vllm.model_executor.offloader.PrefetchOffloader.sync_prev_onload*
        Sync previous onload operations.

        Ensures any H2D copies in flight on copy_stream complete before
        the compute stream continues. Call this before CUDA graph
        capture/replay or when synchronization is needed.

    wrap_modules(modules_generator, prefix='')
    *vllm.model_executor.offloader.PrefetchOffloader.wrap_modules*

                                  *vllm.model_executor.offloader.UVAOffloader*

UVAOffloader
    Bases: `BaseOffloader`

    Offloader using Unified Virtual Addressing (UVA) for zero-copy
    access.

    This offloader moves parameters to pinned CPU memory and creates
    CUDA views using UVA. The GPU can then directly access the CPU
    memory without explicit transfers, at the cost of PCIe bandwidth
    (slower than GPU memory).

    When UVA is disabled via env var, falls back to a
    functional_call-based approach that moves parameters on-demand.

    Parameters: ~
        cpu_offload_max_bytes (int)
            Maximum bytes to offload to CPU.

        cpu_offload_params (set[str] | None, default: None)
            Set of parameter name segments to selectively offload. If
            empty, all parameters are eligible up to the byte limit.

    Methods: ~

    targets       Whether `cpu_offload_params` selects the parameter
                  `param_name`.
    wrap_modules  Wrap modules with UVA offloading.

    _maybe_offload_to_cpu(module, prefix='')
    *vllm.model_executor.offloader.UVAOffloader._maybe_offload_to_cpu*
        Offload module parameters to CPU using UVA if budget allows.

    targets(param_name)
    *vllm.model_executor.offloader.UVAOffloader.targets*
        Whether `cpu_offload_params` selects the parameter `param_name`.

    wrap_modules(modules_generator, prefix='')
    *vllm.model_executor.offloader.UVAOffloader.wrap_modules*
        Wrap modules with UVA offloading.

                              *vllm.model_executor.offloader.create_offloader*

create_offloader(offload_config)
    Create an offloader based on the offload configuration.

    Uses the explicit `offload_backend` selector. When set to `"auto"`,
    selects prefetch if `offload_group_size > 0`, UVA if
    `cpu_offload_gb > 0`, otherwise noop.

                                           *vllm.model_executor.utils._extent*

                                   *vllm.model_executor.utils._in_own_storage*

_in_own_storage(old, new, whole_storage=False)
    `new` copied into the bytes `old` spans if it fits, so the loaded
    storage is kept (with its `data_ptr`); else `new` itself. An
    equal-size result fits too: a repack to the same byte count (e.g.
    FP8 → Marlin int32) then keeps the address captured CUDA graphs
    read.

    With `whole_storage` (direct reload), `new` may use the rest of
    `old`'s storage, so a weight that post-load processing grew keeps
    its address on a reload too, as do a padded view with gaps (ROCm FP8
    padding) and an emptied weight (the checkpoint bytes stay for the
    next reload).

                                      *vllm.model_executor.utils.copy_weight_*

copy_weight_(dst, src)
    `dst.copy_(src)` for weight loaders.

    Model-specific weight loaders should call this instead of `.copy_()`
    when copying a checkpoint tensor to the device. Off integrated GPUs
    it is a plain `copy_`, except that a copy between two byte
    containers (`uint8`, `int8`, `float8_e8m0fnu`, `float4_e2m1fn_x2`)
    keeps the bytes, where `copy_` would convert E8M0 scales by value.
    Float8 value formats still convert by value.

    On integrated GPUs, a host-to-device copy straight from a
    safetensors mmap takes its page faults inside the driver copy, which
    is several times slower than faulting them on the CPU, so touch one
    byte per page of `src` first. PyTorch already stages non-contiguous
    and dtype-converting copies through a CPU temporary. Sources with at
    most one element are skipped: they count as contiguous with any
    stride, which `view(torch.uint8)` rejects.

                                    *vllm.model_executor.utils.get_live_param*

get_live_param(layer, name)
    `getattr(layer, name, None)`, treating retired or empty params as
    absent.

    `get_expert_mapping` method. If the model manually implements
    `get_expert_mapping`, it will be used. Otherwise, it will use the
    first RoutedExperts layer.

                                    *vllm.model_executor.utils.move_parameter*

move_parameter(layer, src_name, dst_name)
    Register the `src_name` parameter object under `dst_name` as well.

    Both names then refer to one object and so to one storage: the
    loader writes through the checkpoint name, kernels read the runtime
    name, and a later `replace_parameter` on either name updates both.
    `dst_name` becomes the name `kernel_parameters` reports for the
    object.

                                    *vllm.model_executor.utils.refill_derived*

refill_derived(obj, name, new)
    >python
        refill_derived(obj: object, name: str, new: None) -> None
<
    >python
        refill_derived(
            obj: object, name: str, new: torch.Tensor
        ) -> torch.Tensor
<
    Set `obj.name` (a plain attribute, never a parameter or buffer) to a
    tensor derived from the weights. A held tensor of the same shape,
    dtype and device is refilled in place, so captured CUDA graphs keep
    its address; it must own its storage. Returns the tensor now held
    under `name`.

                                 *vllm.model_executor.utils.replace_parameter*

replace_parameter(layer, param_name, new_tensor)
    Replace a parameter of a layer while maintaining the ability to
    reload the weight. Called within implementations of the
    `process_weights_after_loading` method.

    The existing parameter object is kept (and so its class and loader
    attributes for weight reloading): `new_tensor` is copied into it
    when shape, stride, dtype and device match, which preserves
    `data_ptr` for captured CUDA graphs; otherwise a smaller
    `new_tensor` is copied into the parameter's own storage (so the
    loaded storage never shrinks), else `.data` is rebound to it. A new
    parameter is registered only if none exists under `param_name`, or
    if the existing one is an online requantization source (released
    after conversion).

    Custom attributes set on `new_tensor` (e.g. kernel dispatch flags
    such as `is_shuffled`) are carried over to the parameter, except
    `weight_loader`, which is always taken from the existing parameter,
    and the direct-reload attributes `_ckpt` and `fill_on_reload`, which
    belong to the parameter they were set on.

    Under direct reload, a `new_tensor` larger than the parameter at
    cold start may be written into the parameter's existing storage on a
    reload, so do not read a local alias of the old data
    (`w = layer.weight.data`) after this call.

    This function should not be called on weights which are tied/shared

    Parameters: ~
        layer (Module)
            Layer containing parameter to replace

        param_name (str)
            Name of parameter to replace

        new_tensor (Tensor | None)
            New data of the new parameter, or None to set the parameter
            to None

                                  *vllm.model_executor.utils.retire_parameter*

retire_parameter(layer, name)
    Mark a loaded parameter that no kernel reads after post-processing.

    It stays registered with its loaded data (so it can be loaded

    configurations.

      *vllm.model_executor.warmup.jit_warmup_triton_helper.TritonWarmupTensor*

TritonWarmupTensor dataclass
    Compile-only tensor metadata used by Triton warmup.

    `strides=None` represents compact row-major storage. Pass explicit
    strides whenever the runtime tensor can be padded, transposed, or
    otherwise strided.

    `ptr_range_bytes` is the byte size of the storage behind the runtime
    tensor (its `untyped_storage()`, not the view), most easily derived
    with `triton_ptr_range`. With buffer ops enabled, Triton's ROCm
    backend gives pointers into storage of at most 2 GB a
    `tt.pointer_range = 32` specialization (32-bit buffer offsets),
    which is part of the compile key. The default 0 assumes such a small
    storage; set it above 2 GB for tensors that view a larger pool, such
    as a KV cache layer, or warmup compiles a variant the runtime never
    uses. CUDA ignores it.

     *vllm.model_executor.warmup.jit_warmup_triton_helper.VllmTritonJitKernel*

*vllm.model_executor.warmup.jit_warmup_triton_helper.triton_scalar_specialization_rep*

triton_scalar_specialization_rep(value)
    Return an integer with the same default Triton JIT specialization.

    For an ordinary integer argument, Triton's cache key contains its
    inferred type (`i32`, `i64`, or `u64`) and one of three value
    classes:

    - `1` is specialized as the exact constant `1`.
    - Multiples of 16 receive a `tt.divisibility = 16` attribute.
    - All other values have no value specialization.

    Warmup only needs one concrete value for each cache-key class. This
    helper returns `1` for the exact-one class and otherwise returns a
    divisible or generic representative while preserving the inferred
    integer type.

    This applies only to non-`constexpr` integer arguments using
    Triton's default specialization. Do not use it for arguments listed
    in `do_not_specialize` or `do_not_specialize_on_alignment`.

    *vllm.model_executor.warmup.jit_warmup_triton_helper.triton_warmup_inputs*

triton_warmup_inputs(kernel, *args, grid, pointer_dtypes=None, **kwargs)

              *vllm.model_executor.warmup.kernel_warmup._aiter_gemm_m_buckets*

_aiter_gemm_m_buckets(max_m)
    One token count per AITER tuned-GEMM bucket up to `max_m`.

    AITER pads M to 1, 2, 4 or 8 below 16, then to multiples of 16 / 32
    / 64 / 128 up to 256 / 1024 / 4096 / beyond, and builds each
    bucket's kernel on first use.

        *vllm.model_executor.warmup.kernel_warmup._load_shared_autotune_cache*

_load_shared_autotune_cache(cache_path, tuner, tune_group)
    Load the per-rank autotune cache into the tuner, group-wide.

    Returns True only when every rank of the tune group had a matching
    file and loaded it: the dummy-run sweep contains collectives, so
    skipping it is safe only if the decision is unanimous.

 *vllm.model_executor.warmup.kernel_warmup._outside_kv_cache_transient_window*

_outside_kv_cache_transient_window(worker)
    Keep a one-off tuning step out of the extensible KV cache's reserve.

    An extensible KV cache keeps free the allocator peak its warmup
    steps reach (`reserved_headroom_bytes`). Autotuning profiles every
    candidate tactic over all token buckets on scratch buffers that
    serving never allocates again, so its peak is not a serving
    transient. Record the transient reached before tuning, then restart
    peak tracking afterwards; the warmup steps that follow run with the
    tuned tactics and measure their own transients.

                *vllm.model_executor.warmup.kernel_warmup.flashinfer_autotune*

flashinfer_autotune(runner, *, skip_attn=False)
    Autotune FlashInfer operations. FlashInfer have many implementations
    for the same operation, autotuning runs benchmarks for each
    implementation and stores the results. The results are cached
    transparently and future calls to FlashInfer will use the best
    implementation. Without autotuning, FlashInfer will rely on
    heuristics, which may be significantly slower.

    Parameters: ~
        runner (GPUModelRunner)
            The model runner to tune.

        skip_attn (bool, default: False)
            Additionally skip attention in the tuning dummy runs.

    With PP > 1, stages run different layers and may profile different
    ops, so each stage's TP group tunes separately with its own cache
    file; otherwise the world group tunes together. Per-tactic timings
    are averaged over the tuning group so all its ranks select the same
    tactic.

    Legacy results are persisted per rank: FlashInfer keys MoE entries
    by tp/ep rank (`MoERunner.get_cache_key_extras`), so one rank's file
    only hits on that rank. A rank with a cache hit skips the per-tactic
    reduce the others block in, so ranks keep loaded configs only if
    every rank in the tuning group has a matching file and successfully
    loads it.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------
                                 *vllm.model_executor.warmup.step5_dsa_warmup*

Warm Step5 DSA scored prefill before serving.

Startup dummy runs are short, so every row selects its whole history and
the indexer scoring path (summary packing, FP8 logits, top-k, page
metadata and, for multi-group caches, staged prefill pages) would
otherwise JIT on the first prefill longer than top-k regions. Under DP
every rank stalls on that rank.

Functions: ~

                                 more than `topk` regions.

    regions.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------
                          *vllm.model_executor.warmup.watermark_sample_warmup*

Warm up the watermarked sampler's Triton kernel.

`_philox_gumbel_kernel` is JIT-compiled once per (key, logits dtype,
skip-mask, `USE_FP64`) specialization. The generic sampler warmup
samples with `SamplingParams.for_sampler_warmup()`, whose feature-heavy
logits processing forces the fp32 copy in `apply_sampling_params`, so
the first ordinary temperature-1.0 request is the first launch with
model-dtype logits and pays the compilation inside inference. This
pre-compiles every specialization the sampler path can launch for the
configured watermark.

              *vllm.model_executor.warmup.watermark_sample_warmup._philox_key*

_philox_key(watermarker)
    None when the watermarker takes the torch path and compiles no
    kernel.

    Philox keys the sampler launches the kernel with.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------
                                                    *vllm.models.deepseek_v32*

DeepSeek V3.2 (`deepseek_v32`) platform entry point.

DeepSeek V3.2 introduced the DeepSeek Sparse Attention (DSA)
architecture: MLA + a "lightning indexer" that selects the top-k tokens
for a sparse MLA attend. The same model code serves any DSA checkpoint,
including GLM-5.2 (`glm_moe_dsa`), which reuses this architecture.

The CUDA and ROCm implementations select capability-specific kernels
internally and fall back when an optimization is unavailable. Other
platforms use the generic implementation by default.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------
                                     *vllm.models.deepseek_v4.common.vl_model*

DeepSeek-V4 vision variant (e.g. DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Vision-Exp).

Thin multimodal wrapper around the text-only `DeepseekV4ForCausalLM`:

- `vision` ViT + `aligner` produce per-image embeddings for the IMAGE
  sentinel positions; four learned vectors (`image_start` / `image_pad`
  / `image_newline` / `image_end`) fill the remaining sentinel
  positions.
- Image placeholders (`<｜deepseek_image｜>`) are expanded by the
  processor in `common/mm_preprocess.py` into sentinel blocks borrowing
  reserved in-vocab tokens `<|place_holder_mm_span_0431|>`..`_0435|>`
  (see `common/vision.py` for the tower itself).
- Merged embeddings enter the text model via `inputs_embeds`, i.e.
  before its hyper-connection stream expansion. Raw `input_ids` still
  flow into the model so the MoE router can apply `bias_vl` to image
  tokens (`requires_raw_input_tokens`).

Classes: ~

                                 *vllm.models.deepseek_v4.DeepseekV4FP8Config*

DeepseekV4FP8Config
    Bases: `Fp8Config`

    FP8 config for DeepSeek V4 with expert-dtype-aware MoE dispatch.

    DeepSeek V4 checkpoints always use FP8 block quantization for
    linear/attention layers. The MoE expert weights vary by checkpoint:
    - `expert_dtype="fp4"` (e.g. DeepSeek-V4-Flash): MXFP4 experts with
    ue8m0 (e8m0fnu) FP8 linear scales. - `expert_dtype="fp8"` (e.g.
    DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Base): FP8 block experts with float32 FP8 linear
    scales.

    The dispatch and the linear scale dtype are both keyed off
    `expert_dtype` from the model's hf_config; missing values default to
    `"fp4"` so existing FP4 checkpoints stay unchanged.

    NOTE: `expert_dtype` is resolved lazily because this config is
    constructed during VllmConfig setup, before
    `set_current_vllm_config` is active. Reading hf_config eagerly in
    `__init__` would always see the default `"fp4"` and silently
    misroute Flash-Base checkpoints.

    _is_quark_mxfp4_ocp(hf_quant_cfg) staticmethod
    *vllm.models.deepseek_v4.DeepseekV4FP8Config._is_quark_mxfp4_ocp*
        True for AMD-Quark exports whose global scheme is MXFP4.

                 *vllm.models.deepseek_v4.quant_config.align_mtp_quant_config*

align_mtp_quant_config(quant_config, config)
    Re-key the quant config's MTP entries onto the draft module
    prefixes.

    `_make_deepseek_v4_weights_mapper` renames the checkpoint's
    `mtp.{i}.` layers to `model.mtp.{i}.`, but the draft modules are
    built under `model.layers.{num_hidden_layers + i}.`. Without this
    remap no per-layer entry matches, so every MTP linear falls back to
    the global scheme. On a mixed checkpoint (FP8 attention and shared
    experts, NVFP4 routed experts) that builds NVFP4 parameters for FP8
    weights and the load then fails a shape assertion.

                                         *vllm.models.deepseek_v41.amd.dspark*

DSpark draft model for DeepSeek-V4.1 (semi-autoregressive speculative
decoding).

See: qwen3_dspark.py for base architecture. This one is specialized to
the DSV4.1 DSpark, which reuses the target model's architecture
similarly to MTP. Its weights ship in the target checkpoint under the
`mtp.{0,1,2}.*` prefix.

To implement non-causal attention, we leverage the sparse attention
implementation to include the future query tokens in the top-k indices
for each query token.

    *vllm.models.deepseek_v41.amd.dspark.DSparkDeepseekV4Model.precompute_and_store_context_kv*
        Insert the sliding-window context KV for every draft layer.

        Mirrors the reference DSparkAttention: each layer derives its
        context KV from the SAME projected target hidden `main_x`, via
        that layer's own `wkv` + `kv_norm` + RoPE + quant, then writes
        it at the layer's context slots.

        `context_slot_mappings` is a per-layer list (each entry is the
        context slot mapping for that layer's kv-cache group, since the
        hybrid manager may place draft layers in different groups).
        `None` (or a `None` entry) runs the projection to reserve
        workspace but writes nothing (profiling).

                                            *vllm.models.deepseek_v41.amd.mhc*

The DSV4.1 delayed mHC seams on ROCm.

On gfx950, `mhc_pre_delayed_overlap` moves the gate projection onto a
side stream, overlapped with the next sublayer. On gfx942,
`mhc_pre_delayed_seam` runs AITER's `mhc_fused_post_pre_delayed`, which
applies the previous sublayer's post, collapses the residual with the
carried pre-mix and computes the next gates in one call, from
`MHC_SEAM_MIN_TOKENS` tokens on seams that have a post block and no
fused norm.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------
                                    *vllm.models.deepseek_v41.amd.mono_decode*

DeepSeek-V4.1 mono decode layer on ROCm CDNA4 and CDNA3
(`--monokernel`).

A decode step's backbone layer -- the attention seam, the attention, its
TP all-reduce, the FFN seam, the MoE and its all-reduce -- runs as two
persistent FlyDSL launches (`mono`, this directory) on the layer's
loaded weights, the TP reductions inside the kernels. Every backbone
layer of the checkpoint runs whole (compress ratio 0, 1 or 2 over
`fp8_ds_mla` records): the first layer and the Engram layers hand K1 a
settled residual, and an index source runs vLLM's compressor and indexer
between the two launches. A layer outside that (an MXFP8 KV cache,
another indexer) keeps vLLM's attention seam and attention and runs the
rest as one launch, the FFN launch, from wo_b's unreduced output. A step
takes the kernels when it is decode only, at most `MAX_ROWS` rows (eager
or a FULL CUDA graph: the model is not torch.compiled); a whole layer
also needs its SWA rows as the kernels read them (causal windows; for
the DSpark draft's layers, the block's non-causal rows). Anything else
runs the layer as before; the paths share every tensor at the layer
boundary, so they interleave freely.

On CDNA3 (gfx942) the kernels compute the same layer on their own copies
of the weights (`mono/weights942.py`), at TP 4 and on steps of up to
`MAX_ROWS_GFX942` rows. An index source's keys are written by
`mono/keylist.py` between vLLM's indexer and K2 there, and the DSpark
draft layers also take the FFN launch, built for the draft's routing.

Every TP rank must take the same path at every layer (the kernels wait
on each other's pushes): the conditions read only metadata every rank
holds alike.

                 is not

             *vllm.models.deepseek_v41.amd.mono_decode._capture_plain_experts*

_capture_plain_experts(experts)
    gfx942: vLLM converts the routed experts to its Triton kernels'
    format when the weights are loaded and frees the plain scales. Wrap
    that step so the gfx942 copies (`weights942.moe_copies`) are made
    from the plain tensors first.

                  *vllm.models.deepseek_v41.amd.mono_decode._copy_942_at_load*

_copy_942_at_load(layer, ffn_only)
    gfx942: the kernels read their own copies of the layer's weights.
    Make them when vLLM processes the weights at load, so that they
    count as model memory when vLLM sizes the KV cache. Copies made at
    the first decode step would count only when that step is also the
    CUDA graph memory profile, so with that profile off or with
    `enforce_eager` they would not count. A layer that takes only the
    FFN launch needs no attention copies.

               *vllm.models.deepseek_v41.amd.mono_decode._copy_linear_at_load*

_copy_linear_at_load(linear)
    gfx942: make the dense MXFP8 linear's `weights942.linear_copy` right
    after vLLM has processed its weights at load. By default
    (VLLM_MXFP8_EMULATION_DEQUANT_AT_LOAD) vLLM dequantizes them to bf16
    there, and the copy re-encodes them as the gfx942 kernels read them.
    Weights that stay e4m3 are copied as they are.

                          *vllm.models.deepseek_v41.amd.mono_decode._gpu_arch*

_gpu_arch()
    The GPU's architecture without its feature flags, for example
    gfx942.

                       *vllm.models.deepseek_v41.amd.mono_decode._keep_copies*

_keep_copies(layer, copies)
    Store a layer's gfx942 copies as `layer.mono942`. A reload of the
    weights (`reload_weights`, or a weight update in RL) runs
    `process_weights_after_loading` again, and the kernels and captured
    CUDA graphs read the first copies by their addresses. So the copies
    of a reload are written into the first copies in place.

            *vllm.models.deepseek_v41.amd.mono_decode._keep_row_major_at_load*

_keep_row_major_at_load(layer, ffn_only)
    gfx950: the kernels read these linears' weights row-major, so their
    kernel keeps them and preshuffles a copy for AITER's GEMMs.

                       *vllm.models.deepseek_v41.amd.mono_decode._mono_runner*

_mono_runner(device, draft=None)
    The process's mono runner (one a TP rank, shared by every layer of
    the target; the DSpark draft's layers share one of their own, as its
    routing and SWA rows differ). Its peer-memory handshake is
    collective over the TP group: every rank builds it at load, at the

----------------------------------------------------------------------------
                                            *vllm.models.deepseek_v41.amd.ops*

gfx942 (MI300X, MI325X) decode helpers for DeepSeek-V4.1.
swa_decode_meta and fused_markov also run on gfx950 (MI355X).

`topk` holds the sparse indexer's top-512 hooks, built from
`topk512_gfx942.cu`, and `cand_logits` the indexer logits of the DSpark
candidate positions. `sparse_indexer` is the indexer layer that runs
them on decode steps. `topk_pack` and `swa_decode_meta` build the decode
attention metadata, `fused_markov` is DSpark's Markov sampling in one
launch, and `draft_lm_head` keeps the DSpark draft's 5-row logits GEMM
off wvSplitK. All of them run only when `enabled()` is true, except
`swa_decode_meta` and `fused_markov`, which run when
`monokernel_cdna3_or_4()` is true.

Modules: ~

                   gfx942.
draft_lm_head      The DSpark draft's base logits on gfx942.
engram_host_table  Engram host tables in HIP VMM host memory, shared across DP
                   ranks by dmabuf FD.
fused_markov       DSpark's sequential Markov sampling with one launch a draft
                   step.
sparse_indexer     The sparse indexer layer of DeepSeek-V4.1 with --monokernel
                   on gfx942.
swa_decode_meta    One-launch decode build of the DeepSeek V4.1 SWA metadata
                   on ROCm.
topk               The sparse indexer's decode top-512 for gfx942
                   (topk512_gfx942.cu).
topk_pack          One-launch packing of the DeepSeek V4.1 decode top-k into
                   global slots.

    _wq_b_uses_aiter_block_scaled cached property

    _decode_topk_ragged(swa_metadata, attn_metadata, num_decodes,
        num_decode_tokens)

        Ragged form of the topk indices this layer's index source
        published.

        The packing depends only on the shared `topk_indices_buffer` and
        per-step metadata, apart from the layer's own compress ratio, so
        the source memoizes one result per ratio for all the layers
        below it.

    _forward_csa2_full(hidden_states, positions)
    *vllm.models.deepseek_v41.amd.rocm.DeepseekV41ROCMAiterMLAAttention._forward_csa2_full*
        CSA layers: one fork replaces the base pipeline's three.

        Each fork/join is a HIP event pair per side stream on ROCm, so
        the base three-fork pipeline is expensive there; the compressor
        chain and the indexer weights projection run fully in parallel
        with the default chain. The indexer K write and q-side stay
        serial after the join: `wk` consumes the aux-0 latent and the
        q-side's wq_b consumes the default-stream qr.

    _forward_csa2_reindex(hidden_states, positions)
    *vllm.models.deepseek_v41.amd.rocm.DeepseekV41ROCMAiterMLAAttention._forward_csa2_reindex*
        Indexer-only layers: the q-side overlaps the SWA q path.

        The input projections run serial first: the q-side consumes qr,
        so it can only overlap the SWA q projection and KV insert.

    _forward_decode(q, positions, kv_cache, swa_metadata, attn_metadata,
        swa_only, output, output_mxfp8=None)

        inverse-RoPE'd.

    _forward_prefill(q, positions, compressed_k_cache, swa_k_cache, output,

    *vllm.models.deepseek_v41.amd.rocm.DeepseekV41ROCMAiterMLAAttention._forward_prefill*
        Sparse prefill into bf16 `output`, or into `mxfp8_out`.

        With `mxfp8_out` the rows go to a bf16 workspace first and are
        then inverse-RoPE'd and quantized into it in one pass.

    _split_qkv_and_norm(qr_kv)
    *vllm.models.deepseek_v41.amd.rocm.DeepseekV41ROCMAiterMLAAttention._split_qkv_and_norm*
        Fuse q/kv RMSNorm + per-1x128 fp8 q quant into one aiter kernel.

        The shared path norms q and kv in one triton kernel and the wq_b
        linears then re-read the bf16 qr to quantize it. The aiter
        kernel computes both RMSNorms (fp32 accumulate) and the fp8
        group quant in a single pass, writing fp8 qr + group scales
        directly; both wq_b GEMMs (attention and indexer) then consume
        that pair and skip their own input quant. kv stays bf16: the
        fused insert kernel RoPE/quantizes it itself. Falls back to the
        shared path when the aiter linear path is not active.

apply_pre_quantized_block_scaled_mm(linear, x_fp8, x_scale)
    Block-scaled fp8 GEMM on pre-quantized activations.

    The fused q/kv norm kernel writes fp8 qr + per-1x128 scales; this
    drives the linear's block-scaled GEMM directly with them, bypassing
    apply_weights which would re-quantize the fp8 input. Only valid for
    the wq_b-style column/replicated linears: their output is the local
    TP shard, so no all-reduce is needed.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------
                                       *vllm.models.deepseek_v41.amd.vl_model*

DeepSeek-V4.1 vision variant.

Thin multimodal wrapper around the text-only
`DeepseekV41LLMForCausalLM`:

- `vision` ViT + `aligner` produce per-image embeddings for the IMAGE
  positions; three learned vectors (`image_start` / `image_newline` /
  `image_end`) fill the delimiter positions. Every image-span position
  carries `image_token_id` (129264) in `input_ids`; the per-position
  roles come from the processor's `types` tensor (see
  `common/mm_preprocess.py`, and `common/vision.py` for the tower).
- Merged embeddings enter the text model via `inputs_embeds`, i.e.
  before its hyper-connection stream expansion. Raw `input_ids` still
  flow into the model so the MoE router can apply `bias_vl` to image
  tokens (`requires_raw_input_tokens`).

    accepts_unnormed_unroped_query property
    *vllm.models.deepseek_v41.attention.DeepseekV4Attention.accepts_unnormed_unroped_query*
        Whether `forward_mqa`'s `q` is the raw `wq_b` output.

        True when the attention kernel applies the Q norm and RoPE
        itself, and reads Q in its own chunk-interleaved layout, so the
        layer only zero-pads Q to `padded_heads` and inserts KV before
        calling it.

    packed_kv_cache_dtype property
    *vllm.models.deepseek_v41.attention.DeepseekV4Attention.packed_kv_cache_dtype*
        The packed KV record this layer's kernel prefers.

        What an unspecific `--kv-cache-dtype` (`auto` / `fp8`) resolves
        to. Mega attention overrides it: its kernel is the one that can
        read an NVFP4 compressed cache.

    _alloc_attn_out(num_tokens, hidden_states)
    *vllm.models.deepseek_v41.attention.DeepseekV4Attention._alloc_attn_out*
        The buffer `forward_mqa` fills, per the interface contract.

    _compressed_kv_cache()
    *vllm.models.deepseek_v41.attention.DeepseekV4Attention._compressed_kv_cache*
        The compressed-KV cache tensor of this layer's kv source (own
        cache for kv-source layers).

    _fused_qnorm_rope_kv_insert(q, kv, positions, attn_metadata)
    *vllm.models.deepseek_v41.attention.DeepseekV4Attention._fused_qnorm_rope_kv_insert*
        Ready `q` for the attention kernel and publish this step's KV.

        One launch does both. With `accepts_unnormed_unroped_query` the
        attention kernel norms and rotates Q itself and reads it in its
        own chunk-interleaved layout, so the Q half of the launch is a
        zero-pad to `padded_heads` -- and nothing at all once the shard
        is that wide. On large eager steps of a `_pads_q_by_copy` layer,
        a KV-only launch leaves that pad to `_pad_interleaved_q`.

    _indexer_cache_cls()
    *vllm.models.deepseek_v41.attention.DeepseekV4Attention._indexer_cache_cls*

        backend. A platform subclass returns one with its own builder.

    _indexer_cls(k_cache)
    *vllm.models.deepseek_v41.attention.DeepseekV4Attention._indexer_cls*

        returns one that writes and scores its own cache layout.

    _o_proj(attn_out, positions) abstractmethod
    *vllm.models.deepseek_v41.attention.DeepseekV4Attention._o_proj*
        Project whatever `_alloc_attn_out` produced through wo_a and
        wo_b.

        Takes the buffer whole, so each layer owns the shape it
        allocated: the bf16 layers slice off their padding heads and
        apply the inverse RoPE, while a layer whose attention kernel
        already did the inverse RoPE and the FP8 cast gets a
        QuantizedActivation and has only wo_a and wo_b left.

    _prepare_and_attn(hidden_states, qr, kv, qr_scale, kv_score,
        indexer_weights, positions, attn_out)
    *vllm.models.deepseek_v41.attention.DeepseekV4Attention._prepare_and_attn*
        Attention input preparation followed by the sparse indexer and
        MLA.

        Only the latter runs in the eager break.

        Q/SWA preparation overlaps state saving and compression. Once
        the latent is ready, main-cache insertion overlaps indexer
        preparation; both cache writes finish before sparse attention
        reads either cache.

    _split_qkv_and_norm(qr_kv)
    *vllm.models.deepseek_v41.attention.DeepseekV4Attention._split_qkv_and_norm*
        Split the fused q-lora / kv projection and RMSNorm both halves.

        Compatible MXFP8 projections share the quantized Q and scales;
        other projection backends consume the normalized Q directly.

                        *vllm.models.deepseek_v41.attention.DeepseekV4Indexer*

DeepseekV4Indexer
    Bases: `Module`

    DeepSeek V4.1 sparse-attention indexer.

    Exists only on `index_source_layer_ids`; consumers reuse the topk
    indices it publishes into the shared `topk_indices_buffer`. Unlike
    v4.0 the index key is derived from the kv-source layer's compressor
    latent (`k = k_norm(wk(latent))`, `owns_k`) instead of an
    indexer-local compressor over hidden states, so there is no
    hidden-state K GEMM here. Non-owning index sources share the kv
    source's paged K cache.

    Two-level candidate filtering: the indexer at
    `candidate_source_layer_id` additionally publishes the top
    `candidate_topk_blocks` blocks of `candidate_block_size` compressed
    positions (`candidate_write`); later indexers mask their scores to
    those blocks before their own top-k.

    Methods: ~

    forward_q  Build the indexer queries: wq_b over qr plus fused RoPE/quant.

    _produce_k(latent, positions, rotary_emb)
    *vllm.models.deepseek_v41.attention.DeepseekV4Indexer._produce_k*
        Turn the compressor's pre-RoPE latent into paged index keys.

        `k_norm(wk(latent))` at group-boundary tokens, RoPE'd at the
        group position and MXFP4/FP8-quantized into the indexer K cache.

    _wq_b_proj(qr, qr_scale=None)
    *vllm.models.deepseek_v41.attention.DeepseekV4Indexer._wq_b_proj*
        Project normalized Q with the main attention's shared
        quantization.

    forward_q(qr, qr_scale, indexer_weights, positions, rotary_emb)
    *vllm.models.deepseek_v41.attention.DeepseekV4Indexer.forward_q*
        Build the indexer queries: wq_b over qr plus fused RoPE/quant.

        Split out so the ROCm layer can schedule it apart from
        `_produce_k` (e.g. on an aux stream once `qr` is ready).

                       *vllm.models.deepseek_v41.attention._pad_interleaved_q*

_pad_interleaved_q(q, out)
    Copy chunk-interleaved `q` [N, H, D] into `out` [N, HP, D].

    Writes the fused KV-insert op's interleaved Q layout: in each 16-dim
    chunk, the H live heads copied bit for bit, then +0.0 in the HP - H
    padding slots. Both tensors are dense and share a dtype; `16 * H`
    and `16 * (HP - H)` must be powers of two.

                     *vllm.models.deepseek_v41.attention._replace_layer_index*

_replace_layer_index(prefix, layer_id)
    Swap the layer index inside a `...layers.<idx>...` prefix.

             *vllm.models.deepseek_v41.attention._resolve_dsv4_kv_cache_dtype*

_resolve_dsv4_kv_cache_dtype(use_fp8_ds_mla_layout, kv_cache_dtype,
    cache_config, packed_kv_cache_dtype='fp8_ds_mla')
    Map `(layout, --kv-cache-dtype)` to
    `(cache_dtype_str, torch_dtype)`.

    Both layouts are paged; they differ in the per-token block format.
    The packed formats are `uint8`-backed: `fp8_ds_mla` is UE8M0
    block-scaled fp8 throughout, `nvfp4_ds_mla` keeps that
    sliding-window record and stores the compressed cache as NVFP4. An
    unspecific `--kv-cache-dtype` (`auto` / `fp8`) resolves to
    `packed_kv_cache_dtype`, the record this layer's kernel prefers, and
    the canonical string is written back onto `cache_config` so the
    page-size specs pick the right per-token slot. Plain-row backends
    store each token's KV row in its element dtype: bf16 or per-tensor
    FP8 E4M3.

                    *vllm.models.deepseek_v41.attention.autotune_indexer_wq_b*

autotune_indexer_wq_b(model, num_tokens)
    Short-context dummy runs skip wq_b, so tune it directly.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------
                                *vllm.models.deepseek_v41.common.vl_cudagraph*

Encoder CUDA graph support for the DeepSeek-V4.1 vision tower.

Mixin implementing the `SupportsEncoderCudaGraph` protocol
(`vllm/model_executor/models/interfaces.py`) on top of the shared
`DeepseekV4ViT`/`DeepseekV4Aligner`. The captured graph packs a whole
batch of images into one varlen run: ViT blocks attend per image via
`cu_seqlens`, and the aligner's spatial merge becomes a gather+mask
against precomputed indices. Span assembly (IMAGE_START/IMAGE_NEW_LINE/
IMAGE_END delimiters) stays eager in `postprocess_encoder_output` but is
batched over all items of the packed batch.

Enabled via `--compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mm_encoder": true}'`; the
manager (`vllm/v1/worker/encoder_cudagraph.py`) handles budget packing,
DP sharding and eager fallback.

                      *vllm.models.deepseek_v41.compressor.DeepseekCompressor*

DeepseekCompressor
    Bases: `Module`

    DeepSeek V4.1 KV/score compressor.

    Pools `compress_ratio` consecutive tokens into one KV latent with a
    learned softmax gate (ratio 1 has no gate and no pooling). Owns the
    linear, norm and state cache. State saving, compression and RMSNorm
    share one Triton kernel. The emitted latent feeds independent
    main-cache and indexer K kernels, which the attention layer can
    schedule concurrently.

    Methods: ~

    forward       Save states and return the BF16 latent for cache insertion
                  and indexing.
    insert_cache  Publish compressed main-cache rows after the latent becomes
                  ready.

    forward(kv_score, positions, rotary_emb=None)
    *vllm.models.deepseek_v41.compressor.DeepseekCompressor.forward*
        Save states and return the BF16 latent for cache insertion and
        indexing.

        Only valid group-boundary rows are written. Under PCP each rank
        pools its own rows and gathers chunk tails to close cross-rank
        groups and keep every rank's rollback ring equal.

    insert_cache(latent, positions, rotary_emb)
    *vllm.models.deepseek_v41.compressor.DeepseekCompressor.insert_cache*
        Publish compressed main-cache rows after the latent becomes
        ready.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------
                              *vllm.models.deepseek_v41.decoder_replay_layers*

Decoder-side SWA bounded replay: running the replay layers on their
batch.

Once the last KV-source layer has written every row's KV, it and the
layers past it (which own only SWA KV) run on each request's last
`window` rows only. `DeepseekV41ModelState` prepares those rows as a
sub-batch with attention metadata and a forward context of its own, like
a microbatch; `DecoderReplayLayers` gathers the layer inputs by its
rows, runs the layers under that context and scatters the outputs back
to batch rows. FULL graphs and small PIECEWISE ones keep the layers on
the whole batch; larger PIECEWISE graphs break out to the replay batch,
which may run in a graph of its own (decoder_replay_cudagraph.py).

Classes: ~

DecoderReplayLayers  Runs the replay layers on the step's replay batch.
ReplayBatch          One forward's replay batch; `run_graph` is set when it
                     runs in a graph.

          *vllm.models.deepseek_v41.decoder_replay_layers.DecoderReplayLayers*

DecoderReplayLayers
    Runs the replay layers on the step's replay batch.

    `run_layers` takes a batch's layer inputs and returns its per-row
    outputs; `write_batch_kv` takes them too and writes the first replay
    layer's KV for every row. `metadata_prefixes` are the attention
    metadata keys the layers read, so the replay batch builds only
    those. `first_swa_prefix` keys the first replay layer's SWA
    metadata, built with the batch's window starts. `has_early_aux`
    tells whether layers before the replay layers capture aux hidden
    states, which the forward holds across the replay layers.

    Methods: ~

                             out to the replay

                                *vllm.models.deepseek_v41.DeepseekV4FP8Config*

DeepseekV4FP8Config
    Bases: `Fp8Config`

    FP8 config for DeepSeek V4 with expert-dtype-aware MoE dispatch.

    DeepSeek V4 checkpoints always use FP8 block quantization for
    linear/attention layers. The MoE expert weights vary by checkpoint:
    - `expert_dtype="fp4"` (e.g. DeepSeek-V4-Flash): MXFP4 experts with
    ue8m0 (e8m0fnu) FP8 linear scales. - `expert_dtype="fp8"` (e.g.
    DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Base): FP8 block experts with float32 FP8 linear
    scales.

    The dispatch and the linear scale dtype are both keyed off
    `expert_dtype` from the model's hf_config; missing values default to
    `"fp4"` so existing FP4 checkpoints stay unchanged.

    NOTE: `expert_dtype` is resolved lazily because this config is
    constructed during VllmConfig setup, before
    `set_current_vllm_config` is active. Reading hf_config eagerly in
    `__init__` would always see the default `"fp4"` and silently
    misroute Flash-Base checkpoints.

    _is_quark_mxfp4_ocp(hf_quant_cfg) staticmethod
    *vllm.models.deepseek_v41.DeepseekV4FP8Config._is_quark_mxfp4_ocp*
        True for AMD-Quark exports whose global scheme is MXFP4.

     *vllm.models.deepseek_v41.sparse_mla.DeepseekV41SparseSWAMetadataBuilder*

DeepseekV41SparseSWAMetadataBuilder
    Bases: `DeepseekSparseSWAMetadataBuilder`

    SWA metadata builder base for v4.1.

    The shared builder classifies decode layer types by the v4.0 ratios
    (1 = SWA-only, 4, 128). v4.1 uses 0 / 1 / 2, so recompute the set of
    tile-scheduler plans from the v4.1 topology.

              *vllm.models.deepseek_v41.sparse_mla.DeepseekV4SparseMLABackend*

DeepseekV4SparseMLABackend
    Bases: `AttentionBackend`

    DeepSeek-V4.1 sparse-MLA backend base.

    Subclasses `AttentionBackend` directly (not the V3.2
    `FlashMLASparseBackend`): DeepSeek-V4.1 runs its own attention layer
    (`DeepseekV4Attention`), so it does not reuse the V3.2 builder or
    impl, and only needs to declare its own metadata builder, KV-cache
    layout, and the sparse-MLA capability flags.

                 *vllm.models.deepseek_v41.sparse_mla.FlashMLAMegaAttnBackend*

FlashMLAMegaAttnBackend
    Bases: `DeepseekV4FlashMLABackend`

    FlashMLA's mega-attention kernel: Q RoPE + sparse attention +
    inverse RoPE + FP8 cast of the output, in one launch.

    Same metadata and KV-cache geometry as `FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV41` --
    what differs is the attention layer's interface contract (it takes
    an unnormed, unroped Q and returns an already-inverse-RoPE'd,
    quantized output) and the extra `nvfp4_ds_mla` compressed-cache
    record only this kernel can read. SM100 only; the kernel has no SM90
    instantiation.

                     *vllm.models.dots3_note.nvidia.vision.PatchMergerAdapter*

PatchMergerAdapter
    Bases: `Module`

    Cybertron `PatchMerger`
    (`pool_kind='patch_merger', proj_kind='identity'`).

    Assumes the encoder output is already laid out in
    `merge_size`x`merge_size` groups (qwen `pre_pixel_shuffle`
    preprocessor + RoPE grouped accordingly), so merging is a simple
    `view(-1, merge**2 * in_dim)` of consecutive tokens. State-dict
    layout matches cybertron's `PatchMerger` (`ln_q` over the per-token
    dim, `mlp.0` / `mlp.2` Linear).

                    *vllm.models.dots3_note.nvidia.vision.PixelShuffleAdapter*

PixelShuffleAdapter
    Bases: `Module`

    Legacy adapter: NHWC pixel-shuffle spatial merge + LayerNorm +
    2-layer MLP.

    Mirrors `cybertron`
    `FCAdapter(pool_kind='pixel_shuffle', proj_kind='mlp2x_ln_gelu')`.
    State-dict keys: `proj.0` (LayerNorm of in_dimmerge*2), `proj.1` /
    `proj.3` (Linear).

                                    *vllm.models.dots3_note.nvidia.vision_moe*

Functions: ~

note_vision_fused_moe_fp8  Run top-k SwiGLU MoE with the encoder's block-FP8

          *vllm.models.dots3_note.nvidia.vision_moe.note_vision_fused_moe_fp8*

note_vision_fused_moe_fp8(hidden_states, w13, w2, topk_weights, topk_ids,
    w13_scale, w2_scale)
    Run top-k SwiGLU MoE with the encoder's block-FP8 formula.

    Unlike vLLM's generic functional MoE path, the native NOTE encoder
    keeps dynamic activation scales as FP32 instead of rounding them to
    E8M0. Weight scales are block 128x128 and activations are quantized
    per token/group-128.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------
                                                           *vllm.models.hy_v4*

HY V4 (`hy_v4`) model --- hardware-isolated entry point.

HY V4 combines three architectural pieces:

- iHC (independent Hyper-Connections): the single residual stream is
  replaced by `hc_mult` parallel residual channels, gated per sub-block.
- MLA + lightning indexer: multi-head latent attention with an optional
  DSA-style sparse top-k selection, plus an output gate and a learnable
  sink.
- MoE: sigmoid-routed experts with a clamped SwiGLU and shared experts.

The package is organized like `vllm.models.deepseek_v32`: this module is
the only public entry point and dispatches on the current platform, so
registry entries never reach into a platform subpackage.

NVIDIA and ROCm are supported, the latter through `amd/`. The port also
drops the reference implementation's HPC/TPCP fusion paths, which depend
on infrastructure that does not exist in this tree.

                         *vllm.models.inkling.InklingForConditionalGeneration*

InklingForConditionalGeneration
    Bases: `_TmlForCausalLMBase`, `SupportsMultiModal`

    Top-level (multimodal) entry point.

    Builds the vision + audio towers on top of the shared text backbone.
    Inkling has NO cross-modal fusion (the vision tower emits one token
    per patch, the audio tower one token per frame), so generation
    reuses the inherited backbone `forward` / `compute_logits` (the
    latter already applies muP) and this class only adds multimodal
    embedding + merge.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------
                                            *vllm.models.inkling2.nvidia.loop*

Looped Inkling2 checkpoints (`loop_config`).

The core layers `[core_start, core_end)` run `num_passes` times: a
prelude, then each pass from the AttnRes state after the prelude, then
the coda from the last pass's state. Each pass of a core layer has its
own KV and conv-state caches. In passes after the first, every core
sublayer input (attention q/k/v and MLP) is blended with a message: a
normalized-value AttnRes read of the previous pass's blocks, merged by a
gated low-rank controller. Each sublayer's short conv runs fused with
the next AttnRes mix (and small batches at TP > 1 with its all-reduce);
without sequence parallel.

                                  architecture name; the model is
Inkling2LoopModel

                                  input: from the rank-`r`

                  *vllm.models.inkling2.nvidia.loop.Inkling2MessageController*

Inkling2MessageController
    Bases: `Module`

    Blends a loop message into a core sublayer input: from the rank-`r`
    projection `h` of the RMS-normalized `[dest, message]`,
    `(1 - tanh(forget(h))) * dest + tanh(gain(h)) * message` in fp32.

    The weights are views of the layer's stream-stacked weights
    (`Inkling2LoopDecoderLayer`), which run every stream at once;
    `forward` is the per-stream reference.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------
                                           *vllm.models.inkling2.nvidia.sconv*

Inkling2 short convolutions with their state kept in a sliding-window
cache.

Each decoder layer owns one `InklingConvState` (shared with Inkling v1)
holding its four conv streams (K, V, attn-out, mlp-out) packed
head-major. K/V are TP-sharded with the KV heads; the attn-/mlp-output
streams are replicated full-width on every rank
(`replicate_hidden=True`).

Classes: ~

                   conv-state stream.

                                                 *vllm.models.kimi_k3.amd.dsa*

Kimi K3.1 DSA (DeepSeek Sparse Attention) for the kimi_k3 stack on ROCm.

Ports `nvidia/dsa.py`: the indexer runs through
`SparseAttnIndexer.forward_hip` (the DeepSeek V3.2 ROCm pattern) and the
sparse MLA layers are served by ROCM_AITER_MLA_SPARSE over the

dropped: the ROCm indexer kernels take the native head count.

                                *vllm.models.kimi_k3.amd.dsa.KimiK3DSAIndexer*

KimiK3DSAIndexer
    Bases: `Module`

    wq/wk/wv indexer projections with FP8 or MXFP4 scoring on ROCm.

    Forward quantizes the indexer query, folds the scales into the
    per-head weights and drives
    `torch.ops.vllm.rocm_aiter_sparse_attn_indexer` via
    `SparseAttnIndexer.forward_hip` with `cache_layout="NORMAL"`: the
    indexer pages are block-flat, which the Triton insert wrapper cannot
    infer from the cache shape alone. MXFP4 uses group scales and
    dedicated FlyDSL scoring with the same global token-index output
    contract.

KimiK3DSAIndexerKNorm
    Bases: `Module`

    numeric change is that weight/bias multiply in the activation dtype.

           *vllm.models.kimi_k3.amd.mla.KimiK3MultiHeadLatentAttentionWrapper*

KimiK3MultiHeadLatentAttentionWrapper
    Bases: `MultiHeadLatentAttentionWrapper`

    Kimi-K3 MLA wrapper with eager AITER q/kv RMSNorm and output gate
    fusions and a fused decode Q-prep path.

    _compute_w_fold(w_qb, w_uk, num_heads, qk_nope_head_dim, qk_rope_head_dim)
    staticmethod
    *vllm.models.kimi_k3.amd.mla.KimiK3MultiHeadLatentAttentionWrapper._compute_w_fold*
        W_fold = [W_UK @ W_qb_nope ; W_qb_pe]: one GEMM gives [ql_nope |
        q_pe].

        `w_qb` is the q_b_proj weight [N * (P + R), Lq], `w_uk` is [L,
        N, P]. Rows hold all heads' nope rows, then all pe rows, so the
        two output halves of `x @ W_fold.T` are contiguous: [B, N * L]
        and [B, N * R].

    _fused_decode(q, kv_c_normed, k_pe, output_shape, attn_metadata, layer,
        kv_cache, slot_mapping)
    *vllm.models.kimi_k3.amd.mla.KimiK3MultiHeadLatentAttentionWrapper._fused_decode*
        Decode-only MLA through one fused AITER launch.

        Replaces the fp8 KV-cache write plus the `[ql_nope | q_pe]`
        concat and that query's static fp8 quant with a single
        `fused_qk_rope_concat_and_cache_mla`. On an untouched upstream
        build the concat and quant already arrive as one inductor-fused
        kernel, so this collapses two launches into one.

                                  *vllm.models.kimi_k3.amd.specialized_decode*

Kimi-K3 specialized decode for ROCm (MI355X, TP8), layer mode: FlyDSL
MonoKernels per MoE decoder layer on pure spec-verify steps (K1 / K2 on

----------------------------------------------------------------------------
                                            *vllm.models.minimax_m3.amd.model*

Inference-only MiniMax M3 (text backbone) model --- AMD ROCm
implementation.

Self-contained per-platform impl (mirrors `deepseek_v4/amd`). It is
identical to `../nvidia/model.py` except for RMS normalization:
FlashInfer's Gemma RMSNorm kernels are CUDA-only, so
`MiniMAXGemmaRMSNorm` here uses a native (FlashInfer-free)
implementation.

  The MiniMax-M3-preview config selects a single set of branches: ~

  - qk_norm_type == "per_head"
  - SwiGLU-OAI MLPs (Transformers reports hidden_act as "silu")
  - use_gemma_norm == True -> Gemma-style RMSNorm everywhere
  - attention_output_gate == False
  - scoring_func == "sigmoid" with a routing-bias correction term
  - "minimax_m3_sparse" layer_types -> a subset of layers run the extra
    "index" attention branch.

                                  partial RoPE.

                                  dense layers).

                                  correction and a shared

                        *vllm.models.minimax_m3.amd.model.MiniMAXGemmaRMSNorm*

MiniMAXGemmaRMSNorm
    Bases: `Module`

    Gemma-style RMS normalization (native ROCm implementation).

    Normalizes in fp32 and scales by `(1 + weight)` --- numerically
    equivalent to the FlashInfer `gemma_rmsnorm` /
    `gemma_fused_add_rmsnorm` kernels used in the NVIDIA path, which are
    unavailable on ROCm. When `residual` is given, the fused add + norm
    returns the updated `(normed, residual)` pair.

    The fp32 normalize + scale + (optional) residual-add run in a single
    fused Triton pass (`amd.ops.gemma_rmsnorm` /
    `gemma_fused_add_rmsnorm`) instead of a chain of elementwise PyTorch
    kernels.

                   *vllm.models.minimax_m3.amd.model.MiniMaxM3SparseAttention*

MiniMaxM3SparseAttention
    Bases: `Module`, `AttentionLayerBase`

    Block-sparse attention layer with the lightning-indexer branch.

    This is a merged attention layer: it owns the projections (qkv +
    index q/k), per-head QK norms and RoPE, and the attention-backend
    wiring that a generic `Attention` layer would normally provide ---
    it binds the `MiniMaxM3SparseBackend` + main impl, registers the
    main paged K/V cache, and owns the lightning indexer
    (`MiniMaxM3Indexer`), which holds the index-key side cache.

    The index branch (index_{q,k}proj + index_norm) feeds the sparse
    top-k block selection. M3 always disables the index value/output
    projections (`sparse_disable_index_value` set for every sparse
    layer), so `index_{v,o}_proj` are never created.

    _emits_o_proj_mxfp8()
    *vllm.models.minimax_m3.amd.model.MiniMaxM3SparseAttention._emits_o_proj_mxfp8*
        Whether this step's attention writes MXFP8 for `o_proj` itself:
        the NVFP4 decode kernel can, `o_proj` takes MXFP8 input, and the
        batch is decode-only (a captured piecewise graph or a mixed
        batch keeps the bf16 output).

    _native_gfx942_qknorm_rope_cache(qkv, positions, fwd_slot_mapping)
    *vllm.models.minimax_m3.amd.model.MiniMaxM3SparseAttention._native_gfx942_qknorm_rope_cache*
        Run QK norm, RoPE, and cache insertion without the fused HIP op.

    *vllm.models.minimax_m3.amd.model._aiter_moe_fused_shared_experts_enabled*

_aiter_moe_fused_shared_experts_enabled(is_fused_shared_expert_enabled)
    Whether the fused shared expert routes through aiter's grouped top-k
    MoE.

    A strict sub-case of `is_fused_shared_expert_enabled`: shared-expert
    fusion must already be opted in
    (`VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS`) and allowed (not under
    expert parallelism). When additionally on gfx950 with an active
    aiter MoE backend, the shared expert is appended inside aiter's
    biased grouped top-k kernel (`num_fused_shared_experts`) instead of
    the vLLM router's torch concat. Otherwise FSE still runs via the
    vLLM top-k bias router.

                          *vllm.models.minimax_m3.amd.model._build_rotary_emb*

_build_rotary_emb(config, head_dim)
    Build the (partial NeoX) RoPE from `config.rope_parameters`.

    Without scaling the cos/sin cache is sized to
    `max_position_embeddings` (524288 native); a request whose positions
    exceed that reads the cache out of bounds and the worker
    hard-crashes (no Python traceback). When scaling is set (e.g. YaRN
    `factor: 2` to reach 1M), it is threaded into `get_rope` so the
    proper scaled embedding is built and its cache covers
    `original_max_position_embeddings * factor` positions. Default
    behavior (no scaling) is unchanged. Shared by the dense and sparse
    attention layers, and the index branch reuses the returned module.

    Note: for the VL checkpoint, set the scaling on the text config
    (`--hf-overrides '{"text_config":{"rope_parameters":{...}}}'`) --
    that is the config the decoder reads here; a top-level override does
    not reach it.

                 *vllm.models.minimax_m3.amd.model._can_fuse_input_norm_mxfp8*

_can_fuse_input_norm_mxfp8(qkv_proj)
    Whether `input_layernorm` can hand `qkv_proj` an MXFP8 activation.

    The quant key does not encode the scale layout (FlashInfer wants
    swizzled scales under the same key), so this also requires a ROCm
    kernel that reads the row-major scales the fused norm writes.

                              *vllm.models.minimax_m3.amd.model._is_moe_layer*

_is_moe_layer(config, layer_id)
    Whether this layer's MLP is a sparse MoE block (vs a dense MLP).

                         *vllm.models.minimax_m3.amd.model._kv_insert_operand*

_kv_insert_operand(t)
    K or V operand for `aiter.reshape_and_cache`, without a needless
    copy.

    The AITER sparse-PA insert takes K and V as column slices of the
    fused `[q | k | v | index_q | index_k]` projection, so they are
    row-strided views and never contiguous. `reshape_and_cache` does not
    need them to be: it passes `key.stride(0)` to the kernel as the row
    pitch and reads `key[token_idx * key_stride + i]` for `i` over
    `num_heads * head_size`, so the only requirement is that the
    trailing `(num_heads, head_size)` block be contiguous within a row,
    which such a slice always satisfies. Any other layout falls back to
    a copy.

                       *vllm.models.minimax_m3.amd.model._mxfp8_linear_kernel*

_mxfp8_linear_kernel(linear)
    The MXFP8 kernel of `linear`, or None.

             *vllm.models.minimax_m3.amd.model._redirect_fused_shared_experts*

_redirect_fused_shared_experts(weights, model)

    experts.

                    *vllm.models.minimax_m3.amd.model._should_skip_index_topk*

_should_skip_index_topk(config, layer_id)
    ATOM `index_topk_freq` (cross-layer index sharing).

    Only 1 of every `index_topk_freq` sparse-attention layers recomputes
    the lightning-indexer top-k block selection; the rest reuse the
    selection the preceding compute layer wrote into the shared
    `topk_indices_buffer` this same forward pass. This cuts the indexer
    score + top-k cost ~`freq`x but approximates the per-layer
    selection, so validate accuracy on long-context inputs. Gated by
    `use_index_cache` in the text config; enable via
    `--hf-overrides '{"text_config": {"use_index_cache": true, "index_topk_freq": 4}}'`.

                *vllm.models.minimax_m3.amd.model._sparse_attention_layer_ids*

         *vllm.models.muse_spark.amd.muse_moe_runner.token_sharded_moe_output*

token_sharded_moe_output()
    Make the TP finalize write only current rank's rows of a
    token-sharded stream.

    Rank `r` keeps rows `[r * R, (r + 1) * R)` with `R = ceil(T / tp)`,
    the rows its reduce-scatter receives; the other rows of the output
    are left unwritten.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------
                                                      *vllm.models.muse_spark*

Muse Spark HF model entry point.

The model classes load on first access, so importing a submodule such as
`common.vision` doesn't import the NVIDIA model. Its kernels import
FlashInfer, which queries the GPU at import and so initializes CUDA in
the importing process; processes forked from it afterwards can't use
CUDA.

Modules: ~

amd     AMD ROCm implementation of Muse Spark.
common  Platform-independent MuseSpark preprocessing.
nvidia  NVIDIA-specific MuseSpark model implementations.

Classes: ~

MuseSparkDSparkForCausalLM        Muse DSpark head with the target's
                                  output-distribution transform.
MuseSparkForConditionalGeneration  Muse Spark Omni: text stack plus NaViT
                                  vision and waveform audio.

                           *vllm.models.muse_spark.MuseSparkDSparkForCausalLM*

MuseSparkDSparkForCausalLM
    Bases: `Qwen3DSparkForCausalLM`

    Muse DSpark head with the target's output-distribution transform.

    Methods: ~

    output_logit_transform_params  `(multiplier, soft_cap)` of
                                   `apply_output_logit_transform`.
    sample_markov_chain            Fuse sampling tails after the ordinary
                                   base-logits projection.

    _sample_sequential_fused(speculator, num_reqs, head_hidden)
    *vllm.models.muse_spark.MuseSparkDSparkForCausalLM._sample_sequential_fused*
        The `sample_sequential` hook under the specialized decode, which
        DSparkSpeculator._sample_sequential asks first: the fused Markov
        sampling loop samples the drafts, and this returns True.

    output_logit_transform_params()
    *vllm.models.muse_spark.MuseSparkDSparkForCausalLM.output_logit_transform_params*
        `(multiplier, soft_cap)` of `apply_output_logit_transform`.

        The fused DSpark Markov loop computes the transform from these
        values (`logits * multiplier`, then
        `soft_cap * tanh(x / soft_cap)` unless `soft_cap` is None)
        instead of calling it, so a subclass that changes the transform
        must override this too.

    sample_markov_chain(speculator, base_logits, prev, idx_map, sample_pos,
        out_tokens, *, prev_indices=None)
    *vllm.models.muse_spark.MuseSparkDSparkForCausalLM.sample_markov_chain*
        Fuse sampling tails after the ordinary base-logits projection.
        Returns each step's Markov embedding, `[rows, steps, rank]`, or
        None when the speculator must run its own loop.
